plan.overview:
Plan for the next FirePlayer update (on top of 1.0.374): Live TV and Multiview. Everything below was checked against the code in /home/user/firestick-player and the six findings.

WHAT ACTUALLY WENT WRONG TONIGHT (it changes the priorities)
- The 12-minute "idle decoder" was not caused by a picture left off screen.
- At 20:51:50 the MediaTek video service (vpud) crashed on damaged H.264 from the channel that kept "ending".
- The player stayed READY and "playing" with a frozen picture, and FirePlayer noticed nothing.
- At 21:04:05 a playlist update released that player. The codec flush timed out and the decoder service wedged until the reboot.
- FirePlayer then built 7 more players on the dead decoder. Each one spun with no words.
- Each close cleared the surface before releasing the player. That made the main thread wait Media3's 2000 ms surface-detach timeout plus its 500 ms release timeout (2.5 s per player). Closing Multiview with 2 stuck pictures froze the screen for 5 s, which caused the ANR.

THE PLAN, IN PRIORITY ORDER
(1) A safe way to let go of a player:
- remove the listener first;
- never clear the surface before release();
- time the release;
- cap Media3's surface wait at 500 ms for live players.
(2) One shared, in-memory "video decoder not responding" state. Once it is set, FirePlayer stops building players by itself, shows the plain message, and never retries ERROR_CODE_TIMEOUT on the same player.
(3) Agreed change 2, extended. A cheap picture watch (one timer every 4 s, reading decoder output counters) covers both the first picture of an open (15 s) and a picture that freezes mid-play. It is shared by the single player and Multiview.
(4) Agreed change 1. When the Home/Search picture has been out of sight for 60 s, the video track is turned off. That frees the hardware decoder while the sound plays on.
(5) The new Multiview layout:
- 3 pictures: 2 on top, the third centred underneath, and a half-size "Add a channel" button to its right.
- 4 pictures: the plain 2x2 grid.
- Gap 8 to 6 dp, corner radius 12 to 8 dp.
- D-pad ties decided the same way every time.
(6) Multiview graphics memory. Today each layout change grows graphics memory by about 14 MB and nothing trims it (measured up to 364 MB). The fix is to draw the corners with an exact rounded-rectangle call, plus a trim after moves.
(7) Less lag when the provider ends a stream:
- reconnect after 50 ms instead of 300 ms;
- a decoder error gets its own quick retry;
- a test-gated option that queues a second copy of the channel, so the next connection takes over while the loaded tail plays out.
(8) Plain words for replies that aren't a video stream, fewer status rebuilds, and playlist names kept out of the log.

Lean and compatible:
- Nothing runs per frame and nothing starts at app start-up. The only new timers run while a channel is open (one main-thread check every 4 s; one shared check for all Multiview pictures).
- No new dependencies, background jobs, preferences or database changes. Old and new versions stay compatible both ways.
- New logic sits in pure, unit-tested classes: LivePictureWatch, DecoderHealth, LiveOffScreen, LiveChain, the MultiviewLayout changes, and LiveReconnect/LiveRefusal additions.
- Every item has a Max check. The stuck-decoder paths can't be produced on demand, so they are checked with a test-only build that blocks the live video renderer (never committed).

layout_spec.screen:
The Max at 1920x1080 px with density 2 (1 dp = 2 px). MultiviewLayout works in dp on a 960 x 540 dp board (Multiview.layoutNow divides the board size by density). MultiviewBoard.settle rounds each box to whole px once, when a move ends. New constants:
- LiveWidths.MV_GAP 8f -> 6f (12 px). It is both the screen-edge margin and the gap between pictures.
- LiveWidths.MV_RADIUS 12f -> 8f (16 px).
- New private const ADD_SCALE = 0.5f in MultiviewLayout.
Every picture stays 16:9 (ASPECT). Two rows of 16:9 pictures on a 16:9 screen can be at most 270 dp tall, so in the grid only the smaller gap can add space; the grid is already height-bound.
layout_spec.one_tile: Unchanged. One picture (the moment Multiview opens, or a single tile) is Box(0,0,960,540) dp = 1920x1080 px. Removing pictures down to one still leaves Multiview for full screen on that channel (MultiviewRules.leaveAfterRemove).
layout_spec.two_tiles:
Side by side, centred, as wide as the screen allows:
- cw = (w - 3g)/2 = 471 dp, ch = cw*9/16 = 264.9375 dp.
- Boxes (6, 137.53125, 471, 264.9375) and (483, 137.53125, 471, 264.9375) dp.
- In px: 942x530 at (12,275) and (966,275). That is 48.2% of the screen (was 936x527 at (16,277) and (968,277), 47.5%).
Nothing larger is possible for two 16:9 pictures side by side.
layout_spec.three_tiles:
Default 'In a grid' with no large picture. Same cell size as the 2x2 grid, so a picture keeps its size between 3 and 4.
Cell size: ch = (h - 3g)/2 = 261 dp, cw = ch*16/9 = 464 dp. Grid left = (w - (2cw + g))/2 = 13 dp, top = (h - (2ch + g))/2 = 6 dp.
- Picture 0 (top-left): Box(13, 6, 464, 261) dp = 928x522 px at (26,12), spanning to (954,534).
- Picture 1 (top-right): Box(483, 6, 464, 261) dp = 928x522 px at (966,12), spanning to (1894,534).
- Picture 2 (bottom, centred): left = (w - cw)/2 = 248 dp. Box(248, 273, 464, 261) dp = 928x522 px at (496,546), spanning to (1424,1068).
- 'Add a channel' button: only when hasAdd (3 pictures, no large one, the setting allows 4). See add_channel_button.
Pictures cover 70.1% of the screen, Add 5.8% (was 68.5% and 22.8%).
With 'Up to 3' the bottom picture is still centred and there is no Add.
Code: in MultiviewLayout.of, for count == 3 and featured == null, use cells[0], cells[1] and Box((w - cw)/2, cells[2].top, cw, ch) instead of cells[2]. Add = addBeside(bottom, w, gap) when hasAdd.
layout_spec.four_tiles:
The plain 2x2 grid as today, with gap 6:
- (13,6), (483,6), (13,273), (483,273) dp, each 464x261 dp.
- In px: 928x522 at (26,12), (966,12), (26,546), (966,546).
- 93.4% of the screen (was 917x516 px, 91.3%).
Going from 3 to 4: the centred bottom picture slides left to (26,546) over 260 ms (translation/scale only), the new 4th appears at (966,546), and Add hides. Going from 4 to 3: the bottom-left picture slides to the centre and Add fades in after half the move (MultiviewBoard.place already does this from layout.add).
layout_spec.corners_and_fit:
- Corner radius 12 dp (24 px) -> 8 dp (16 px) on every picture. The selection ring's inner edge follows automatically (MultiviewBoard.ring uses the same radius).
- What the corners hide: per corner 124 px² -> 55 px², and the diagonal inset 7.0 px -> 4.7 px. So broadcaster logos and clocks in the corners are nicked about 56% less.
- The corners are still the board's black painted over each picture's corners (no outline clip). On API 29+ (the Max is API 30) they are drawn with Canvas.drawDoubleRoundRect (outer rect, radius 0; inner rounded rect, radius r), which the GPU draws exactly. The even-odd Path is kept only for API < 29. This also fixes the GPU-cache growth (see item mv-gpu-memory).
- The video is still fitted, never cropped: the surface takes the video's shape inside the picture, with VIDEO_SCALING_MODE_SCALE_TO_FIT and black bars where the shapes differ.
- The ring stays 3 dp, white, outside the picture. Margins and gaps of 6 dp keep it on screen and off the neighbouring picture.
- MINI_RADIUS (12 dp, the guide miniature and the ready picture) is unchanged. The 12 -> 8 dp step when Multiview opens is a small visual difference.

items.title: Safe release order and shorter Media3 waits for every live and Multiview player
items.user_ask: Fewer glitches FirePlayer can correct by itself; keep the app quick (tonight: 2.5 s freezes per close and the ANR on closing Multiview)
items.tests:
New DecoderHealthTest (pure):
- a release of 449 ms isn't slow; 450 ms is;
- slow-release marks the state; a first frame anywhere clears it.
The close order can't be unit-tested (it is Media3 behaviour); it is covered by code review plus the Max checks.
Existing MultiviewLeasesTest and LiveSessionTest must still pass (lease order is unchanged: the player goes before the lease).
items.lean_impact: Each healthy close does one codec operation less on the playback thread and one main-thread wait less. Worst case on a stuck decoder: 2.5 s to 0.5 s per player; closing Multiview with 2 stuck pictures 5.0 s to 1.0 s, with 4 pictures 10 s to 2 s, all under the 5 s ANR limit. No memory, CPU or start-up change.
items.risk: Low. A healthy release takes about 50-150 ms (log 20:35:01.690 to .738; 22:21 three releases in 230-450 ms total). If a release ever times out at 500 ms but finishes later, the next player on the same SurfaceView could fail to connect its decoder. That case also sets DecoderHealth, so the picture watch says so instead of spinning. A 500 ms surface wait is far above a healthy detach (a few ms).
items.verify_on_tv:
Max, with logcat filtered to FirePlayerLive, ExoPlayerImpl, Choreographer and AmazonKeyEventLogging:
- 20 channel up/down zaps; Multiview open, add 3rd and 4th, remove, Change channel, close; Home key; Movies tab; back to Live TV.
- Expect: no 'Live recovery: ERROR_CODE_TIMEOUT' or 'Multiview recovery' lines on closes; no 'Skipped N frames' above 30 near a Release; every channel still shows its first frame on the reused surface; key latency under 300 ms on close.
- A test-only build (never committed) whose live video renderer blocks 10 s in onDisabled: the close must cost at most about 0.5 s per player, and log the slow-release line.

items.title: One shared 'video decoder not responding' state; ERROR_CODE_TIMEOUT never retried on the same player; no automatic players while stuck
items.user_ask: Less glitches FirePlayer can correct by itself; part of agreed change 2 (a plain message instead of an endless spinner)
items.change:
DecoderHealth object: main thread, memory only, never stored.
- Fields: stuck: Boolean, why: String.
- markStuck(why), noteSlowRelease(ms), pictureShown() (any first frame in any player clears it), canBuild(byViewer) = !stuck || byViewer.
- const TEXT = "The TV's video decoder isn't responding\nA restart of the Fire TV may be needed" (39 and 38 characters, 2 lines at 13 sp in the 340 dp busy box).
It is set by:
- a release of 450 ms or more;
- a ThreadBeat (player/ThreadBeat.kt, one per player on p.playbackLooper) silent for 3 s or more while a stream is open;
- an ERROR_CODE_TIMEOUT reaching a listener (after item release-order, only real ones arrive);
- the picture watch's DECODER verdict.
PlayerHost:
- onPlayerError (647-681) handles ERROR_CODE_TIMEOUT before anything else: log 'Live recovery: the player's own thread isn't answering (ERROR_CODE_TIMEOUT)', letGo the player (player = null; the lease and channel are kept), markStuck, no reconnectAfter.
- New Status field stuck: String? = null (a data-class default, so existing callers still compile), set while stuck for the playing key.
- openStream gets byViewer. tune() passes byViewer = pressedAt != 0L or an explicit pick. session.resume via onScreenStarted, backAfterUpdate, warm() and streamDead re-tune pass false. When !DecoderHealth.canBuild(byViewer): no player is built, Status.stuck = TEXT, publish.
- Before the first live player of a process: warm() calls DecoderCheck.ask(), and openStream waits with DecoderCheck.whenAnswered(10_000, ready = open, stuck = { markStuck("decoder list") }), as films do (PlayerActivity.kt:1216-1226).
Screen:
- HomeActivity.showBusy (1478-1487): when status.stuck != null, busy.show(spinning = false, text = stuck, still = true). New BusyOverlay mode: overlay visible, ProgressBar GONE, label shown.
- keepScreenOn (1456) also needs stuck == null.
- The PiP page says it once through the pipErrorSaid path (1462-1467).
- LivePage treats stuck like error: no automatic full screen (2290); OK or channel change tries once (pick 1441); the Play/Pause and held-Back guards (2345, 2436, 2478).
Multiview:
- MultiviewPlayer.onPlayerError: ERROR_CODE_TIMEOUT -> letGo, error = DecoderHealth.TEXT, markStuck.
- Multiview.begin/enterWith (140-170) and addPicture refuse with callbacks.notice(TEXT) while stuck.
- resume() and startTile don't open tiles while stuck; their tile shows TEXT through refresh().
- Change channel (a viewer action) tries once.
items.lean_impact: Two booleans and a string in memory. It prevents the pile-up seen tonight: 7 players on a dead decoder, each leaking a playback thread, a loader thread, a socket with about 1.3 MB unread, and its buffer. No start-up cost: DecoderCheck.ask() runs on its own thread when Live TV warms its player, and the codec list is built then anyway.
items.risk: Low to medium. A false 'stuck' would block automatic resume until a picture shows. Mitigations: viewer actions always try once more; any first frame clears it; the thresholds sit far above healthy values (release 50-150 ms vs 450; decoder start 33-138 ms vs 15 s).

items.title: Agreed change 2 (extended): first-picture watchdog at 15 s and frozen-picture recovery, single view and Multiview
items.user_ask: When a channel shows no picture within ~15 s, stop spinning and say the TV's video decoder isn't responding; also catch tonight's silent 12-minute freeze
items.change:
LivePictureWatch (pure, modelled on player/PictureWatch.kt). Constants: FIRST_MS 15_000, FROZEN_MS 12_000, SILENT_MS 3_000, CHECK_MS 4_000, SPARSE_WINDOW_MS 120_000.
API: opened(now) (a stream opened, a jump, or video turned back on); check(now, wanted, tracksKnown, hasVideo, decoderStarted, frames, playing, threadSilentMs): Verdict; recovered(now).
frames = rendered + skipped + dropped from p.videoDecoderCounters, or -1 when there is none. Skipped frames count while the surface is hidden, because Media3 then decodes into its placeholder. A frame counts as shown when frames > 0 and differs from the last look, so a new decoder starting again from 0 still counts.
Verdicts:
- DECODER: thread silent >= 3 s; or 15 s after opened, with a video track known but onVideoDecoderInitialized never came.
- NO_PICTURE: 15 s with the decoder started but 0 frames out.
- NO_DATA: 15 s with no tracks yet (network or provider, never blamed on the decoder).
- FROZEN: frames were shown, then none for 12 s while isPlaying with video selected. Only once per stream; a second freeze within 2 min after frames came back marks the stream sparse (a still-picture channel), and it is no longer judged for freezes.
- Never judged: no video track (radio), not wanted (paused, parked, video deliberately off, error, refused or stuck shown).
PlayerHost:
- New pictureCheck Runnable, posted every 4 s while a stream is open.
- watch.opened() in openStream after p.prepare() (538-540), in retry (612), behind-live-window (652), the goLive seek (372) and when video comes back (item offscreen-decoder). A small startJump() helper sets jumping = true together with it.
- decoderStarted is set in the existing bandwidth listener's onVideoDecoderInitialized (730); onRenderedFirstFrame also calls DecoderHealth.pictureShown().
- Stopped in closeStream, parkPaused, on error, refusal and stuck.
Actions:
- DECODER: markStuck; letGo; Status.stuck; cancel retry; log 'Live: no picture 15 s after opening (tracks at X ms, decoder started: no); the TV's video decoder isn't responding'.
- NO_PICTURE: the first time, letGo and open the same source on a fresh player. The second time, a per-channel message, 'This channel isn't sending a picture right now', with LiveRefusal's slow tries; not global.
- NO_DATA: reconnectAfter('no data 15 s after opening', "Can't reach the channel's server", ended = false), so 'Reconnecting…' and the existing back-off apply instead of a silent spinner.
- FROZEN: log 'Live recovery: the picture stopped (no new frames for 12 s; sound playing|ended)'; letGo; reopen the source once on a new player, which the first-picture watch then covers.
Multiview:
- One shared Runnable in Multiview.kt every 4 s calls tile.player.check(now) for each tile (not one timer per picture).
- MultiviewPlayer holds a LivePictureWatch and a ThreadBeat per player.
- DECODER -> error = DecoderHealth.TEXT and markStuck; NO_PICTURE -> the same per-channel line; FROZEN -> the picture's player is reopened (this was the device's 57-minute frozen bottom-left picture); NO_DATA -> its reconnectAfter.
- Add a log line per picture on its first frame: 'Multiview: a picture shown in N ms (decoder M ms)'.
items.lean_impact: Nothing per frame. While a channel is open: one main-thread Runnable every 4 s (in Multiview one for all pictures) reading 3 player fields and posting one empty message to the playback thread. Memory: a few longs per player. No storage, no start-up cost. It also frees resources sooner: a frozen picture no longer holds a decoder for 12+ minutes or keeps the TV awake on a still frame.
items.risk:
Low to medium.
- A channel with a still picture and moving sound could trip FROZEN: one recovery, then the sparse rule stops it.
- A slow server is never blamed on the decoder: no tracks means NO_DATA.
- 15 s is 3.5 times the slowest start measured (4.4 s).
items.verify_on_tv:
Max:
- 20 zaps and 30 min on one channel, PiP on Home, and a radio channel if the playlists have one: no verdict lines in the log.
- The channel that answered 'container unsupported': it says 'Reconnecting…' or the plain line, never a silent spinner past 15 s.
- A test-only build that silently disables the video track (without the off-screen flag): FROZEN recovery within about 16 s and the picture back within about 2 s.
- The test-only blocking-renderer build: the decoder message after about 15-19 s, in single view and on a Multiview picture.
- Multiview with 3 pictures for 20 min: one 'shown in N ms' line per picture, and no false reopen.

items.title: Agreed change 1: let go of the hardware video decoder after the picture has been out of sight for 60 s (sound plays on)
items.user_ask: Release a live channel's hardware video decoder when its picture has been off screen for a while instead of holding an idle decoder
items.change:
HomeActivity owns the 'seen' signal, because only it knows whether the surface shows.
- New private noteSeen(v: Boolean), which calls player.setPictureSeen(v) only when the value changes.
- Seen = surface VISIBLE, and either not on Home/Search PiP, or PipRules.pictureShows with a hole that isn't null and isn't above pipClip, and Multiview not open.
- Call sites: settleVideo (1337-1360), hideVideo (1315-1334: INVISIBLE, so false), showPipShift / showPipSizing / showPipHole (656-685; a null hole, or a hole above pipClip, is false; only a boolean compare on that path) and setMultiview (372-377).
PlayerHost.setPictureSeen(seen):
- false: postDelayed(dropPicture, LiveOffScreen.AFTER_MS = 60_000).
- true: remove it; if videoOff, pictureBack().
dropPicture runs only when LiveOffScreen.dropDue(...) says so: a stream is open, not paused or parked, !DecoderHealth.stuck, frames moved within the last 10 s (only a healthy decoder is let go; releasing a dead one is what hangs), and not already off. It then:
- sets videoOff = true;
- applies p.trackSelectionParameters.buildUpon().setTrackTypeDisabled(C.TRACK_TYPE_VIDEO, true); Media3 then resets the video renderer and releases the codec on the playback thread, with no main-thread wait;
- logs 'Live: picture out of sight 60 s, its video decoder let go (sound plays on)'.
pictureBack():
- videoOff = false; startJump() (jumping = true and watch.opened, so the stall watch and picture watch don't misjudge it);
- re-enables the video track;
- logs 'Live: picture back in N ms' at the first frame.
A plain TS stream may reconnect to reach a keyframe (about 1 s; the spinner shows after 300 ms).
Also:
- openStream resets videoOff (a new channel is shown with video) and re-arms dropPicture if still unseen.
- PiP Full screen and held Back call setPictureSeen(true) before the grow (settleVideo already does).
- The picture watch skips while videoOff.
- Multiview needs nothing: its pictures are always on screen, and the single player is stopped while it is open.
- Pause stays as today (a paused plain stream is parked after 10 min).
items.lean_impact: Frees one hardware decoder, its output buffers (about 12 x 3.1 MB, roughly 37 MB, for a 1080p picture, measured with SurfaceFlinger) and the decode and composition CPU. Device measurement on Home scrolled away: 23-30% app CPU with the decoder running. Sound and connection are kept. Costs one main-thread timer only while the picture is out of sight. No storage.
items.risk:
Low to medium.
- Returning after more than 60 s costs about 1 s with the spinner (keyframe or reconnect).
- Captions and the chosen audio track are separate track types and are kept, but must be checked.
- The status videoSize goes UNKNOWN while off; HomeActivity then lays the hidden surface out at 16:9, which is harmless.
items.verify_on_tv:
Max: FirePlayer Home with the live tile.
- Scroll the rows so the tile is out of view and wait 70 s: the log line appears; the media.codec 'MtkOmxVdecDecod' thread count drops to 0 (the device investigator's method); the audio track stays active (dumpsys audio); app CPU drops.
- Scroll back: the picture returns in about 1-1.5 s ('picture back in N ms').
- Open a title page for 30 s and come back: nothing is dropped (under 60 s).
- Repeat with captions on and a non-default audio language: both kept.
- PiP Full screen after a drop: the picture comes back before or during the grow, with no black screen beyond about 1 s.

items.title: Multiview layout: 3 = 2 on top + centred bottom + half-size Add button; 4 = 2x2 grid; gap 6 dp; corners 8 dp; predictable D-pad
items.user_ask: For 3 Multiview screens centre the bottom screen with a smaller 'Add channel' button to its right; the 4th makes the normal grid; use more free space; keep rounded edges but slightly less cropped
files: app/src/main/java/app/fireplayer/live/ui/MultiviewBoard.kt (KDoc only, plus the corner draw in item mv-gpu-memory)
items.change:
Constants:
- LiveWidths.kt:90 MV_GAP 8f -> 6f.
- LiveWidths.kt:110 MV_RADIUS 12f -> 8f (update its KDoc; MINI_RADIUS stays 12f).
MultiviewLayout.of (MultiviewRules.kt:44-51), for count == 3 and featured == null:
- tiles = [cells[0], cells[1], Box((w - cw)/2, cells[2].top, cw, ch)];
- add = if hasAdd, addBeside(bottom, w, gap).
New private addBeside(b, w, gap):
- aw = min(ADD_SCALE*b.width, w - gap - (b.right + gap)); ah = aw/ASPECT;
- Box(b.right + gap, b.top + (b.height - ah)/2, aw, ah);
- private const ADD_SCALE = 0.5f.
move() (MultiviewRules.kt:103-122): 'if (score < bestScore - TIE)' with private const TIE = 0.5f, so exact ties go to the earlier stop.
4 pictures, 2 pictures and the large layout keep their maths; only the gap changes.
Update the KDoc: MultiviewRules.kt:9-13, :24, :37; MultiviewBoard.kt:30-36 and :174 ('the grid's free cell' becomes 'the Add button beside the bottom picture'); the MV_ADD comment at LiveWidths.kt:96.
Multiview.kt:472 (the held window's area uses MV_GAP) needs no change.
Exact px and dp are in layout_spec.
items.lean_impact: None: pure maths run once per layout change, with the same views and animations. Pictures are 1-2.4% larger in area (no measurable memory change). The Add cell is a quarter of its old area.
items.risk: Low. Pure, unit-tested code; no prefs or DB change, so old and new versions stay compatible. On a TV with uncorrected overscan the ring sits 2 dp closer to the edge.
items.verify_on_tv:
Max, Multiview:
- with 2, 3 (grid) and 4 pictures, then OK for the large one: screencap each; check bounds with 'dumpsys activity top' against layout_spec (e.g. AddCell 1436,677-1900,938; bottom Picture 496,546-1424,1068).
- D-pad: walk every direction from each stop with 3 pictures.
- 3 -> 4 -> 3: the bottom picture slides, and Add fades in and out.
- Pixel-probe a corner: about 4-5 px dark inset on the diagonal.
- The ring stays fully on screen at the edges.

items.title: Multiview graphics memory: draw the round corners exactly and trim the drawing cache after moves
items.user_ask: Optimise Multiview so FirePlayer stays lean for memory
items.change:
Device measurement:
- each layout change (OK on a picture) grew graphics memory by about 14 MB: 178 MB -> 275 MB after 10 changes, 364 MB in the user's hour-long session;
- 'Scratch: Texture 117 MB (475 entries)', 144 MB of it purgeable;
- nothing in Multiview trims it.
The likely cause: Picture.dispatchDraw (160-166) fills an anti-aliased even-odd Path while the picture is scaled every frame of the 260 ms move. That makes the GPU renderer build a mask texture per transform: about 16 frames x 3 pictures per change, which matches the 475 entries.
Fix 1: on API 29+ draw the corners with canvas.drawDoubleRoundRect(outerRect, zeroRadii, innerRect, radiusRadii, cornerPaint). The GPU draws that exactly, with no mask textures. Keep the Path for API < 29. The RectF and radii arrays are made once per size in onSizeChanged (152-158), so nothing is made per frame.
Fix 2: in moveEnd (318-325) and when Multiview closes, ask GraphicsTrim once.
- If GraphicsTrim.staleOnly (Fire OS 8 on the Max): postDelayed(trimStale, GraphicsTrim.STALE_MS + 1_000), cancelled by the next move.
- Otherwise GraphicsTrim.trim(minGap = 10_000).
- Only on small-RAM TVs (GlassLoad.smallRam), as PlayerActivity does (PlayerActivity.kt:1431-1514).
items.tests: No unit test for the drawing itself (an Android Canvas). Optionally add a pure helper cornerRadii(radius) test. Device measurement is the real test.
items.lean_impact: High for memory: it should keep Multiview graphics near the fresh 117 MB instead of growing by 100-250 MB on a 1.7 GB TV with about 158-200 MB free. CPU: fewer texture uploads during moves. One delayed Runnable per move, nothing per frame.
items.risk: Low. Same look, with corners drawn exactly. The trim drops only resources unused for 30 s.

items.title: Shorter gaps when the provider ends a stream or a decoder error hits
items.user_ask: Less channel lagging (tonight one channel 'ended' 31 times in 15 min, about 0.93 s frozen and silent each time; Multiview pictures about 3.8 s)
items.change:
1. LiveReconnect.ENDED_FIRST_MS 300 -> 50 (LiveReconnect.kt:62). At STATE_ENDED everything loaded has already played out, so the wait buys nothing. A provider still closing its last connection is already handled by LiveRefusal's one quick try.
2. failed(now, ended, decoder = false). A decoder failure (codes in PlayerHost.CANT_DECODE: DECODER_INIT_FAILED and DECODING_FAILED) gets its own first quick wait, DECODER_FIRST_MS = 300, once per steady period, instead of the shared back-off (tonight 2 s after a stream end 3 s earlier: 2790 ms of black). attempt still counts, so the CANT_DECODE_TRIES give-up rule (PlayerHost.kt:666) stays as it is. PlayerHost and MultiviewPlayer pass decoder = e.errorCode in CANT_DECODE.
3. A measurement for the next step: in PlayerHost's bandwidth AnalyticsListener, add onLoadCompleted for DATA_TYPE_MEDIA on plain streams. It logs one line per provider close, 'Live: the provider ended the stream with N ms loaded ahead', from p.totalBufferedDuration. Logged once per connection, never per frame.
items.lean_impact: About 250 ms less freeze per provider close (about 8 s over tonight's 31), and about 1.7 s less black after a decoder error. No memory or CPU change.
items.risk: Low. A provider that refuses an instant reopen shows up as a failed try, which the existing back-off and LiveRefusal already handle.
items.verify_on_tv: Max: watch a channel that drops (or the Multiview bottom-right one from the device session) for 15 min. 'playing again after N ms' should average about 0.65-0.7 s instead of 0.93 s. Check the new 'ended the stream with N ms loaded ahead' values (they decide whether item chain-on-close is worth it).

items.title: Seamless take-over when the provider closes a plain stream (queue a second copy of the channel); ship only if the Max test passes
items.user_ask: Less channel lagging; less glitches FirePlayer can correct by itself
items.change:
How it works:
- Plain TS streams only (LiveTiming kind TS or 'stream', not HLS or DASH).
- When the media load completes (the provider closed the connection; the onLoadCompleted from item ended-faster) and LiveChain.shouldChain(kind, mediaItemCount == 1, playedMs >= 5_000, chainsLastMinute < 6) is true, call p.addMediaItem(liveMediaItem(source)).
- Media3 loads the next period once the current one is fully buffered and its duration has been set at load completion (MediaPeriodQueue.shouldLoadNextMediaPeriod, ProgressiveMediaPeriod.onLoadCompleted, both checked with javap). So the new connection opens while the 1.5-3 s already loaded plays out.
- The new period starts on a keyframe (SampleQueue needs one) and has its own timeline. So there is no ENDED, no decoder flush, no spinner, and no confusion from the provider's PTS jumps.
- In onMediaItemTransition(reason AUTO): removeMediaItem(0) and log 'Live: the provider ended the stream (N ms loaded ahead); the next connection took over'.
- An item that played under 5 s, or more than 6 chains a minute, isn't chained: it reaches ENDED and today's back-off applies, so it can't loop.
Unchanged: setMediaItem on a channel change clears the queue; retry, Go live and behind-live-window act on the current item; ConnectionBudget is untouched (the old connection is already closed).
Build it behind a single private const switch, set true only after the Max test passes; otherwise ship the item with the switch false (only the log from item ended-faster stays).
items.lean_impact: No extra connection, at most one extra MediaItem and period while the tail plays, and no per-frame work. It removes a decoder flush per provider close, and the audio output re-created each time (36 AudioTracks tonight).
items.risk: Medium. Media3 playlist behaviour for live progressive items with no known length has to be confirmed on the Max. If the new connection's first data takes longer than the loaded tail (this provider sometimes needs 1-4 s), the viewer still sees a short buffering wait, but no ENDED or reconnect.
items.verify_on_tv:
Max: a channel that the provider ends regularly (tonight's 720p channel or the device session's bottom-right one), 15 min.
- Expect the 'took over' lines in place of 'stream ended; try 1'; no 'Flushing' lines for the video codec at each close; no AUDIOINFO AudioTrack per close; the screen never black.
- Also zap, Go live, pause and Multiview with a chained item, to check nothing breaks.

items.title: Max checks before release: screensaver, software decoding with 4 pictures, CPU per thread
items.user_ask: Analyze Multiview and keep it lean; less glitches
items.change:
1. Pause a channel and let the Max's screensaver start: onStop and 'ExoPlayerImpl Release' should follow. If not, add a dynamic ACTION_DREAMING_STARTED/STOPPED receiver, registered only while Live TV plays, that acts like onStop/onStart.
2. With 4 Multiview pictures, check which decoders are created (no 'Ffmpeg' or software video decoder). If one appears, Multiview players get a renderers factory with the extension video renderer off and decoder fallback off, so NO_DECODER shows instead of a software picture.
3. top -H per thread, full screen and with 3 pictures, before and after this update, to attribute the about 45% system CPU.
items.lean_impact: Measurement only, unless a check fails.
items.verify_on_tv: As described; record the results in the release notes for the next round.

dropped.idea: Fall back to software decoding (FFmpeg or c2.android.avc) when the hardware decoder is stuck
dropped.why: There's no evidence the 4-core Max can play 720p60 or 1080p in software, it would load the CPU on a 1.7 GB TV, and a Fire TV restart is the real cure. The plain message is clearer and costs nothing.

dropped.idea: A 'connection kill switch' data source that closes a stuck player's sockets from another thread
dropped.why: Closing from another thread while the playback thread is blocked in native code risks races and double closes. Once the decoder is stuck no new players are built, and a Fire TV restart frees everything anyway. Low value for the risk.

dropped.idea: Reconnect inside the data source at end of input (splice the new connection into the same stream)
dropped.why: It feeds the MediaTek decoder a cut H.264 stream with no flush, and tonight damaged H.264 crashed the vendor video service. It also mixes the provider's -6.7 to +10.4 s timestamp jumps into one timeline. The queued-copy approach (chain-on-close) starts each connection on a keyframe in its own period instead.

dropped.idea: Skip the codec flush before release with a renderer subclass that calls releaseCodec() first
dropped.why: It is unproven on the Max. Tonight the move to Idle also hung, not only the flush. And the same disable path keeps the decoder for reuse on channel changes, which a wrong flag would break.

dropped.idea: Reconnect a stall with setMediaItem(same) + prepare() instead of stop()
dropped.why: The small gain isn't worth it: re-creating the decoder after a stall is a useful reset on damaged channels, and the change is untested on the Max.

dropped.idea: Raise the live codec's maximum size to 1920x1088 so 720p<->1080p changes reuse the decoder
dropped.why: It costs roughly 20 MB more of video buffers on 720p channels to save about 100 ms on some channel changes. Channel changes are dominated by the provider (tracks at 0.6-4.4 s).

dropped.idea: Hand the full-screen player to the first Multiview picture and back, instead of release and reopen
dropped.why: Two classes own players today, so the lease, listeners and surface would have to move exactly once each way. That is a medium-to-large change with ANR and black-frame risk; the gain is one reconnect on open and close.

dropped.idea: Upgrade Media3 to 1.10/1.11 for video dynamic scheduling, and 1.9+ stuck-player detection
dropped.why: It is a dependency change beyond this update. Stuck detection runs on the playback thread itself, so it can't fire when that thread is blocked in MediaCodec (tonight's case), and its default limit is 10 minutes.

dropped.idea: Release players on a background thread, or build live players on their own looper
dropped.why: Media3 maintainers advise against it (hardware codecs held for an uncontrolled time, ExoPlayer issue 4352). The bounded 500 ms waits plus the shared stuck state give most of the benefit with a small change.

dropped.idea: Open the next connection before the provider closes the stream (pre-reconnect at about 80% of the drop interval)
dropped.why: It needs a second simultaneous connection. The user's playlists allow one or a few streams, so it would be refused or would eat Multiview's allowance.
Flush and release still run synchronously on the playback thread, so it doesn't help hangs, and it adds threads per codec.

dropped.idea: Round the fitted video's own corners (letterboxed channels)
dropped.why: It adds cropping, the opposite of the user's 'slightly less cropped' request.

dropped.idea: Try to get 1080p Multiview pictures composited in hardware (CLIENT -> DEVICE) by changing the corner overlay or the SurfaceView Z order
dropped.why: The corners are drawn in the UI layer, not on the video layer. The likely limit is the Max's hardware composer capacity for video layers, which the app can't change. It would need a long experiment with no clear lever.

dropped.idea: Change the 'One large on top' proportions (small ones 4 across, or a column on the right)
dropped.why: It changes the user's agreed design, so it is kept as an open question rather than done unasked. This update only trims the gap there.

dropped.idea: Count only decoder failures (not stream ends) toward the CANT_DECODE give-up rule
dropped.why: Both engine investigators say to keep the rule as it is. The decoder's own first quick retry already fixes the 2 s wait seen tonight.

open_questions: Should 'One large on top' stay as it is (small ones sized for 3 across, 344 px of black at each side), or use the free space? Option B: small ones sized for 4 across, large 1391x782 px, small 465x262 px. Option C: small ones in a column on the right, large 1424x801 px.
In 'One large on top' with 3 pictures there is still no 'Add a channel' button (as today). Should a small one go to the right of the bottom row, like the new grid layout?
Is half the picture's size (464x261 px) right for the 'Add a channel' button, or should it be smaller (for example 0.4, 371x209 px)?
Up from the centred bottom picture: go to the top-left picture (fixed rule), or back to whichever top picture you came down from?
Is 60 s out of sight the right delay before the hidden live picture lets go of its decoder (the sound keeps playing)?
OK to test the 'next connection takes over' option on the Max with a channel the provider keeps ending, and to ship it only if it plays through without a freeze?
If turning off the sound of silent Multiview pictures saves a clear amount of CPU, is a sound switch about 0.3-0.5 s slower when you move between pictures acceptable?

verdicts.issues:
1) setDetachSurfaceTimeoutMs(500) does more than shorten a wait. In Media3 1.8.0, ExoPlayerImpl.setVideoOutputInternal waits only when it replaces an output that isn't null, and on timeout it calls stopInternal(ExoPlaybackException.createForUnexpected(new ExoTimeoutException(3), 1003)). I checked this in the bytecode. So a detach that is slow but healthy now stops the player with ERROR_CODE_TIMEOUT where today 2000 ms would have succeeded. That happens on surfaceDestroyed when HomeActivity.hideVideo sets the surface INVISIBLE (HomeActivity.kt:1315-1334), and when attach() switches surfaces. Item decoder-health then turns that error into the global 'restart your Fire TV' state. The plan gives no Max measurement of healthy detach times; 'a few ms' is only asserted.
2) Dropping clearVideoSurfaceView in the playerFor swap (PlayerHost.kt:577-584) removes the step its own comment says exists 'so the new player takes the same surface cleanly'. If release() times out at 500 ms, the old codec is still connected to the SurfaceView's buffer queue. The new player's codec configure then fails, which is DECODER_INIT_FAILED, which is in CANT_DECODE. After 2 tries the viewer sees 'This TV can't play this channel's picture' on a channel that is fine.
3) Multiview.closeAll (Multiview.kt:186-192) releases every tile inside one main-thread message (dropTile, then release, then releasePlayer). Even bounded, 4 x 500 ms is 2 s with no input handled.
4) A 450 ms 'slow' threshold sits on the healthy range: the plan's own evidence has three healthy releases at 22:21 taking 230-450 ms in total under load.
verdicts.amendment:
- Measure first, with a test-only build that times setVideoSurfaceView, clearVideoSurfaceView and release() over 50 zaps, Home/PiP hides, and Multiview with 2-4 pictures on the Max. Set the live detach timeout to about max(1000 ms, 4 x the measured p99) instead of a fixed 500.
- Keep today's proven close order (clear, remove listener, release) for a healthy player. Skip the clear only when the player is suspect: its ThreadBeat has been silent for 1 s or more right then, or DecoderHealth.stuck is set. That removes the 2 s wait exactly where it happened tonight, without changing thousands of healthy closes.
- Always remove the listener first, as planned.
- Count a release as 'slow' only when it actually reached Media3's release timeout (took >= 500 ms). Anything under that is a normal slow release, so drop the 450 ms threshold.
- In Multiview.closeAll and suspend, post each tile's release as its own main-loop message, so key events can run between them.
- A detach timeout on its own marks only that player as failed (one reconnect on a new player), never the global stuck state, unless its ThreadBeat confirms the thread is silent.

verdicts.issues:
1) A false 'stuck' is costly. It blocks the automatic resume in onScreenStarted, which is the quick channel return the user relies on. It shows 'A restart of the Fire TV may be needed' on a healthy TV, and only a viewer action or a first frame clears it. Its triggers are close to healthy values: a 450 ms release (see release-order), a detach timeout made more likely by the 500 ms cap, and a DECODER verdict that misfires (see picture-watch).
2) Gating openStream on DecoderCheck adds a serial MediaCodecList build before the first live connection of every process. Today only PlayerActivity asks (PlayerActivity.kt:668, 1217); Live TV never does, and Media3 builds the list on the playback thread in parallel with the network. The first channel of the day gets slower.
3) 'Viewer actions always try once' allows one player per press while the decoder is stuck. Each such player leaks a blocked playback thread, a loader, a socket with about 1.3 MB unread and its buffer, the pile-up seen tonight. Ten zaps give ten leaks.
4) ThreadBeat posts to p.playbackLooper. After letGo the looper has quit, so a note to it is never answered and the beat reads as silent forever. If the beat isn't dropped at letGo, it sets stuck by itself.
5) pictureShown() fires on any first frame in any player, so in Multiview one healthy picture's reconnect clears a stuck state another picture set. The state can flip back and forth.
verdicts.amendment:
- Set stuck only on:
  - a release that actually timed out (took >= the release timeout);
  - a ThreadBeat of a player with an open stream, silent for 3 s or more;
  - the amended DECODER verdict from picture-watch.
- Self-clear: after a timed-out release, keep a reference to that player's playback thread (playbackLooper.thread) and check Thread.isAlive once about 5 s later. If the thread has ended, the decoder was not wedged: clear stuck and log it. This is one delayed check and costs nothing per frame.
- While stuck, a viewer action may build a new player only when no earlier stuck-era player still has a live, blocked playback thread. Otherwise it shows the message again with no build, so at most one player is ever leaked.
- Drop each player's ThreadBeat at letGo.
- Call DecoderCheck.ask() from warm(), which runs while the last channel is being read. openStream does not wait for it. If it hasn't answered 10 s after asking, markStuck('decoder list'). The ThreadBeat already catches a player that blocks on a stuck list. If the user still wants the films-style gate, log the time openStream waited and keep the gate only if the Max shows a median of 0 ms.
- In Multiview, only a first frame on the picture that set stuck clears it, or a single-view first frame.

verdicts.issues:
1) The DECODER verdict ('a video track known but onVideoDecoderInitialized never came') misfires when PlayerHost reuses its player ('player reused' in the timing line). Media3 keeps the codec across channel changes: MediaCodecRenderer.onDisabled flushes rather than releases, and canReuseCodec reuses it. So no init callback comes for the new channel. A channel that sends no keyframe for 15 s would then get the global 'restart the Fire TV' message instead of the per-channel line.
2) FROZEN_MS = 12 s is only 1.6 s above the provider's measured +10.4 s timestamp jumps. During such a jump video frames wait for their time while the sound plays, so a healthy channel would be torn down and reopened.
3) FROZEN and NO_PICTURE recovery call letGo on a decoder that isn't producing. That is exactly the release that wedged the decoder service at 21:04:05. So FROZEN may itself put the TV into the stuck state within seconds of a vendor-service crash. It must not then rebuild automatically.
4) 'Sparse' is per stream, but the FROZEN reopen starts a new stream and resets the watch. A still-picture channel then gets a false reconnect on every open.
5) The 4 s Runnable keeps posting while paused (up to 10 min before parking) and while not wanted. That is wasted wake-ups.
6) NO_DATA forces a reconnect at 15 s even while Media3's own load retries (LiveErrorPolicy, 3 tries, 10 s connect timeout) are still under way. This doubles the handling and restarts the 15 s clock each time.
verdicts.amendment:
- Base DECODER only on:
  - ThreadBeat silence of 3 s or more (tonight's block in codec creation is on the playback thread);
  - or DecoderCounters showing input queued with 0 output, on two fresh players in a row.
  Read the counters (decoderInitCount, queuedInputBufferCount, rendered+skipped+dropped), not the init callback, so a reused codec counts as started.
- Everything else with no picture is NO_PICTURE, per channel.
- FROZEN_MS = 20 s, and no freeze judgement within 30 s of a position discontinuity or a video format change.
- Key 'sparse' by channel for the life of the process (a small in-memory set), not by player.
- FROZEN and NO_PICTURE reopens go through openStream with DecoderHealth.canBuild(false) and the timed letGo, so a wedged release shows the message instead of building again.
- Post the check only while the stream is wanted: not while paused, parked, videoOff, in error, refused, stuck, or while the screen is stopped.
- NO_DATA: only update the waiting text ('Can't reach the channel's server') at 15 s. Call reconnectAfter only if !p.isLoading, meaning Media3 has given up its own tries.

verdicts.issues:
1) Turning the video track back on in a plain TS stream (ProgressiveMediaPeriod) almost always needs a reset, because the video sample queue was discarded while it was disabled. A reset reconnects the stream and also drops the loaded sound, so there is a sound gap on return as well as about 1 s of spinner. With a provider that allows one connection, it can be refused for a moment and show 'This channel isn't available'. This lands on 'quick channel return' (Home to Live TV after 60 s), which the user relies on.
2) While video is off, Status.videoSize goes UNKNOWN and Status.video goes null. HomeActivity.videoSizeListener then calls layoutVideo() twice (HomeActivity.kt:1474-1477): once to 16:9 when the picture is dropped, and once back when it returns, where a 4:3 channel visibly jumps. LiveControls.kt:303 shows nothing for video.
3) The first frame after pictureBack goes through onRenderedFirstFrame into timing.firstFrame, which can log a misleading 'Channel shown' line.
verdicts.amendment:
- While videoOff, keep the last known videoSize and video format in Status, so nothing re-lays out.
- Start pictureBack at the first sign of a return, not only when the picture is seen: the Live TV tab focused, Home's live row coming into view, PiP Full screen or held Back. This hides most of the reconnect.
- If the reconnect on return is refused, retry quickly and silently once before LiveRefusal speaks.
- Mark the return as a jump in LiveTiming so it logs 'picture back in N ms' and not 'Channel shown'.
- Add Max checks for the sound gap on return, and for a one-connection playlist on return.
- Keep 60 s as the open question; the rest of the design stands.

verdicts.issues:
1) The TIE tolerance fixes nothing. move() already uses a strict 'score < bestScore' (MultiviewRules.kt:119), so an exact tie already goes to the earlier stop. I checked by hand: Up from the centred bottom picture gives 737 for both top pictures, so it goes to 0; Down from the large picture gives a tie at 321 vs 639, so it goes to the first small one. The plan's 'fixes the tie Down from the large picture' is not a real bug. A tolerance quietly lets earlier stops win near-ties everywhere.
2) The new layout creates a regression on 3 to 4. Today the 4th picture takes the Add cell and nothing moves. Now the centred picture (496-1424 px) slides left while the new 4th picture appears at once at 966-1894 px, so they overlap for the first frames. The fix sits in mv-polish part 1, which is only a 'could'.
3) Top-right Down goes to Add, not the bottom picture, though the bottom picture overlaps it by 229 dp. That is a behaviour the user should confirm.
verdicts.amendment:
- Drop the TIE constant. Keep the new D-pad tests, which pin today's strict-less-than behaviour.
- Move mv-polish part 1 (new pictures stay INVISIBLE until moveEnd when others are moving) into this item as a must.
- Add 'top-right Down: Add or the bottom picture?' to the open questions.
- Everything else (the maths, the constants, the tests, the KDoc) stands.

verdicts.issues: The cause is a likely theory, not yet proven. It does fit: an anti-aliased even-odd Path, drawn under a new scale every frame, gives a mask per transform, which matches 475 'Scratch: Texture' entries. The fix costs nothing per frame: the RectF and radii are made in onSizeChanged, and there is one delayed Runnable per move, cancelled by the next. GraphicsTrim on the Max is the 'stale only' way, so only resources unused for 30 s go. Condition: ship Fix 1 only if the Max shows the growth gone and identical corners. If it doesn't help, keep the Path and ship only the trim.

1) The decoder quick retry is keyed on CANT_DECODE, which won't catch tonight's case. The 20:40:55 line is 'Live recovery: ERROR_CODE_DECODING_FAILED; try 2 in 2000 ms', and DECODING_FAILED is not in CANT_DECODE (PlayerHost.kt:864-869 lists DECODER_INIT_FAILED, DECODER_QUERY_FAILED, DECODING_FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED and DECODING_FORMAT_EXCEEDS_CAPABILITIES). The plan's text says it is. If an implementer adds DECODING_FAILED to CANT_DECODE to match, a damaged-stream error would give up after 2 tries with 'This TV can't play this channel's picture'. Today it is retried for as long as the viewer stays.
2) For the real CANT_DECODE codes (all decoders in use, mostly in Multiview), a 300 ms retry spends one of the 2 allowed tries before another picture's decoder is freed. The picture gives up sooner with 'no decoder'.
3) ENDED 50 ms has not been tested against a provider that refuses while its last connection closes. LiveRefusal's first retry is 1 s, so one refusal costs more than the 250 ms gained. Tonight's 31 reopens at 300 ms all worked.
verdicts.amendment:
- Give the quick first retry (300 ms, once per steady period) to a separate set: DECODING_FAILED only. Leave CANT_DECODE and its give-up rule untouched.
- Use ENDED_FIRST_MS = 50 only after 15 min on the Max with the dropping channel shows no 4xx or refusal after an end. Otherwise use 150 ms.
- The onLoadCompleted measurement line stays.

verdicts.issues:

2) Not confirmed: how Media3 1.8 reports a load error of the queued item while item 0 is still playing. If it is held back or ends quietly, the channel could reach ENDED with no reconnect, or show an error late.

verdicts.amendment:

- Add to the Max test: the queued item's connection refused (a one-connection playlist while another device holds it), Live TV buffer change, pause/park and Multiview, each with an item queued.
- Confirm in the log that a failed queued item ends in today's 'stream ended; try 1' path.

verdicts.issues: LiveRefusal.shown is 'code != 0', and message() prints 'The provider answered $code'. A not-a-stream failure has httpCode 0, so as described it can never be shown. PlayerHost's log line 'the channel the provider refused (${refusal.code}) plays' would print 0. Otherwise it is lean and fewer requests are sent.

verdicts.issues: Lean and low risk. The caption path has its own onCues/setCues. The busy, reconnect and Go live signs ride on state, isPlaying and isLoading events, which still publish. verdicts.issues:

Every move of the sound to a picture unselected for 5 s or more would black out or spin that picture for about 1 s, not 0.3-0.5 s. HLS restarts loading too.

verdicts.issues:

EQUAL at 960x540 is a size many HLS ladders don't have, so 928x522 px tiles would fall to 854x480. Each change of limitVideo on a layout change also switches tracks.

verdicts.issues: Making 'All playlists' the one kept big list means opening a single playlist's All channels has to read and hold the union of every playlist. Tonight that is 16,587 + 8,983 + a third playlist. Today ScopeLists keeps only whichever big list was used last (ScopeLists.kt:39-47). So both the first-read time and the memory held while Live TV is open would go up, when the user may only browse one playlist.
verdicts.amendment:

verdicts.issues:
1) The guide reuse rests on a misreading. The two 12.9 MB guide downloads were separate update runs 30 min apart for different playlists: 20:33:58 with 3711 ids, 21:04:17 with 1340 ids. Reuse within one run wouldn't have saved anything. Doing it would need either an in-memory parsed guide (heavy on a 1.7 GB TV) or a union of the wanted refs written to two sources in the stored-guide path.
2) Zap-group pruning needs an order that isn't stored, so a new key plus a copy of sp.all. The benefit hasn't been measured. Writing prefs.focus 'only when focus settles or Live TV is left' must still survive the process being killed.

verdicts.amendment:

- Part 2: first measure the size of the prefs file and the count of zap_group keys on the Max; prune only if it is large. Debounce the focus write (about 1 s after focus settles) and write again when Live TV is left.
- Part 4: park a seekable window only once it has been paused longer than the provider's window (the dynamic window's duration plus a margin), when resuming would land at live anyway.
- Keep parts 3 and 5.

verdicts.issues:
- A reconnect on a feed slower than real time throws away the partly refilled cushion and jumps to live. The same slow feed then rebuffers again.
- It overrides the cushion the user chose with the Live TV buffer setting.
- Repeated stalls use up LiveReconnect's quick tries, so the channel drops to 'Trying again every 30 seconds'.
- There is no evidence that a reconnect refills faster from this provider.
verdicts.amendment:

- Then measure on the Max whether a reconnect refills faster, meaning the provider sends a burst at connect.
- Turn it on only if it does, and never let it count toward the slow tries.

verdicts.issues:
- Part 2's fallback would also turn off FFmpeg audio decoding in Multiview: setExtensionRendererMode(EXTENSION_RENDERER_MODE_ON) covers audio and video together (PlayerFactory.kt:322-324), so channels whose sound only FFmpeg decodes would lose their sound.

missing: Measure the Media3 surface detach and release times on the Max before choosing any timeout value. Today's 2000 ms and 500 ms defaults are known to work on healthy closes.
The ThreadBeat lifecycle: drop it at letGo and never post to a quit looper. A released player's beat would otherwise read as permanently silent and set the stuck state by itself.
A self-clearing stuck state: check once, about 5 s later, whether a timed-out player's playback thread has exited (playbackLooper.thread.isAlive). If it has, clear stuck.
Cap the players leaked while stuck: no new build while an earlier stuck-era player's playback thread is still alive, even on a viewer action.
Release Multiview pictures one main-loop message at a time on close and suspend (Multiview.kt:186-230), so key events are handled between releases.
Keep the last known videoSize and video format in PlayerHost.Status while the video track is off, so HomeActivity doesn't lay the surface out twice (HomeActivity.kt:1474-1477).

Max checks of a one-connection playlist for every new automatic reopen (ENDED 50 ms, offscreen return, FROZEN/NO_PICTURE reopen, chain-on-close): none may turn into a 'This channel isn't available' message.
A test that DECODING_FAILED keeps today's unlimited retries, so the CANT_DECODE give-up rule isn't widened by accident.
A guard that the picture-watch and DecoderHealth logs never include a channel name, playlist name or link (the same rule as the 'a picture' wording in MultiviewPlayer).
critiques.layout_issues:

- Down from the large picture onto 2 small ones: |dx| = 159 for both, so it goes to the first.
Drop the constant and keep the tests.

2) The new 3-picture layout creates an overlap on 3 to 4 that doesn't exist today, where the 4th takes the Add cell and nothing moves. The centred picture (496-1424 px) slides left while the new 4th picture appears at once at 966-1894 px. mv-polish part 1 (new pictures INVISIBLE until moveEnd) must ship with mv-layout.

3) With 3 pictures, top-right Down goes to Add (score 505), not the bottom picture (737), although the bottom picture overlaps the top-right one by 229 dp horizontally. The user should confirm this, alongside the Up question already listed.

4) I checked every box in the spec by hand: grid 13/483, 6/273, cells 464x261; centred bottom at 248; Add Box(718, 338.25, 232, 130.5); two pictures 471x264.9375 at top 137.53; large Box(172, 6, 616, 346.5) with small ones at 358.5. assertSane holds. The ring (3 dp) sits inside the 6 dp edge margin, so 3 dp is left on an overscanned TV. The Add button is 10 dp from the right edge.

5) Keep maxVideo unchanged. Role LARGE also applies when count <= 1 (MultiviewRules.kt:214), so mv-polish part 3 would cap a full-screen Multiview picture at 720p.

6) The radius going from 12 to 8 dp while MINI_RADIUS stays 12 dp gives a visible corner change when Multiview opens. That is acceptable, but it belongs in the Max screencap check.

verdicts.issues:
Mostly right, checked against the Media3 1.8.0 bytecode. ExoPlayerImpl.release() runs internalPlayer.release() (bounded by the release timeout), then sends onPlayerError(ERROR_CODE_TIMEOUT) to listeners if that timed out, and only after that calls removeSurfaceCallbacks(). So removing the listener first does stop the stray error. The log confirms the stray retry: 21:05:49.648 'Live recovery: ERROR_CODE_TIMEOUT; try 1 in 1000 ms' is followed 1 ms later by 'Release c674fc5', and 'Skipped 151 frames' (2.5 s) comes from clear plus release. Problems:
(1) Step 3 is wrong. setVideoOutputInternal waits detachSurfaceTimeoutMs whenever the current output is non-null and different from the new one (bytecode offsets 1-42). So setVideoSurfaceView(new) over an old surface waits exactly as long as clear-then-set does. Skipping clearVideoSurfaceView in PlayerHost.attach (207-212) or MultiviewPlayer.attach (117-122) moves the wait, it doesn't remove it.
(2) Step 4 is a no-op. MultiviewPlayer.playerFor (167) reuses the player when the headers match, so there is often no old player to release. Step (a) already covers the late-error case.
(3) Capping the detach wait at 500 ms makes real ERROR_CODE_TIMEOUTs (from surfaceDestroyed on Home, hideVideo going INVISIBLE, or attach) four times more likely on a busy but healthy decoder. Item decoder-health then turns every such timeout into a global 'stuck', and noteSlowRelease at 450 ms does the same. Two eager triggers combine into a false 'restart your Fire TV' message.
(4) Smaller points: moveEnd is MultiviewBoard 329-337, not 318-325. 'Took >= 450 ms' should log only, not mark stuck.
verdicts.amendment: Drop step 3: it doesn't help. If a stuck player must not touch the surface, skip attaching that player at all. Drop step 4. Keep (a)-(f) and setDetachSurfaceTimeoutMs(500). Make a slow release and a detach-surface ERROR_CODE_TIMEOUT mark the decoder only as 'suspect'. Only a confirming signal (the next ThreadBeat still silent, or the next player's decoder not starting in time) may promote that to stuck. Add a Max check: Home key and zapping during a codec start must not show the stuck message.

verdicts.issues:
(1) 'pictureShown(): any first frame in any player clears it' is too broad. In Multiview, a picture whose decoder was made before the wedge keeps producing first frames after its own reconnects, so it clears the state while new decoders still hang. Automatic builds resume and the pile-up returns.
(2) A ThreadBeat silent for 3 s does not mean the video decoder failed. player/ThreadBeat.kt and FreezeWatch.kt document the playback thread blocking in Fire OS's stuck sound output (seen on the Plus with the HDMI off). There this item would show 'The TV's video decoder isn't responding' and block automatic players, while FreezeWatch shows pause/play or a new player fixes it. Also, with ThreadBeat's one-note design and a 4 s check, silence is only detected 4-8 s after the hang, not at 3 s.
(3) 'Viewer actions always try once more' has no limit. DECODER does letGo (player = null), so every zap builds a new player. On a wedged decoder each one leaks a blocked playback thread, a socket left in CLOSE_WAIT and a buffer: tonight's 7-player pile-up, but driven by key presses.
(4) DecoderCheck caches answered=true for the life of the process and only builds the MediaCodecList. Tonight's wedge got 'OMXClient obtained, never makeComponentInstance', so the list most likely answers and the gate catches nothing. It also turns openStream into an async path while LiveSession.Engine.open is synchronous, and closeStream, stop and a new tune would all have to cancel the pending wait.
(5) A new Status.stuck field plus about 8 call-site edits duplicates what Status.error already does: LivePage pick 1441 re-tunes when error != null, the auto full screen at 2290, the Play/Pause and held-Back guards at 2345/2436/2478, keepScreenOn at 1456, pipErrorSaid at 1462-1467, and showBusy's waiting needs error == null. PlayerHost.streamDead() also retries on error.
(6) Missing: Multiview's board.keepScreenOn stays true while every picture shows the message.
verdicts.amendment: Clear stuck only on a first frame from a decoder whose onVideoDecoderInitialized or decoderInitCount came after markStuck. Mark stuck only on a video-decoder-specific signal: a video track known but no decoder start, a release timeout, or thread silence while the video decoder is starting. For thread silence after frames were playing, use FreezeWatch's neutral path, not the decoder text. Allow at most one viewer-triggered build per stuck episode until the last blocked player's thread answers again (or 30 s pass). Put the message in Status.error (the existing field) instead of a new stuck field. Leave DecoderCheck out for live, or note that it only covers the Plus start-up deadlock and specify how the wait is cancelled. Turn off the Multiview board's keepScreenOn when every tile shows an error.

verdicts.issues:
(1) FROZEN calls letGo on a decoder that has stopped producing frames. Tonight that is exactly what wedged the decoder service: vpud segfaulted at 20:51:50 ('Fatal signal 11 ... name: vdec_srv >>> /vendor/bin/vpud', H264_decode+1212), and the 21:04:05 release of that player caused the FlushInputPort timeout and the wedge. With this item the wedge would come 12 s after the freeze, and 'picture back within about 2 s' won't happen. The plan's own offscreen item says releasing a dead decoder is what hangs.
(2) MultiviewPlayer has no AnalyticsListener, so 'decoderStarted' isn't available there. The plan needs to add one or read DecoderCounters.decoderInitCount, which costs nothing.
(3) Counters written on the playback thread are read on main; call DecoderCounters.ensureUpdated() before reading.
(4) The ThreadBeat must be dropped in letGo. Otherwise posting to a released player's quit looper logs 'sending message to a Handler on a dead thread' every 4 s and the silence keeps growing.
(5) The split into DECODER / NO_PICTURE / NO_DATA, with only DECODER showing the agreed decoder message, is a defensible refinement but changes agreed change 2 ('no picture within ~15 s -> plain decoder message'). It must be put to the user, not decided silently.
(6) The Multiview shared Runnable's start and stop (closeAll, suspend, resume) isn't specified.
verdicts.amendment: Send FROZEN's release through the timed letGo with DecoderHealth 'suspect'. Say in the risk section that after a vendor decoder crash the expected outcome is the decoder message, not a recovered picture. Use DecoderCounters.decoderInitCount (after ensureUpdated) for decoderStarted in both players. Drop the ThreadBeat in letGo. Start the Multiview check Runnable in enterWith/resume and remove it in closeAll/suspend. Add an open question telling the user that network-type no-picture cases will say 'Reconnecting…' or 'This channel isn't sending a picture right now' rather than the decoder text.

verdicts.issues:
The release mechanism is confirmed in 1.8.0: reselectTracksInternal calls enableRenderers, which calls RendererHolder.reset() on every renderer not enabled in the new selection, so onReset releases the codec. But RendererHolder.disable first runs MediaCodecRenderer.onDisabled, which calls flushOrReleaseCodec and flushes first. So the 'healthy decoder only' gate is essential, not optional.
(1) Bringing the picture back on a plain TS is effectively always a reconnect, sound included. ProgressiveMediaPeriod.selectTracks needs sampleQueue.seekTo(position) to find a video keyframe at or before the position, which a disabled queue discarded up to the position almost never holds. seekToUs on unseekable media then goes to 0 and restarts the load (ProgressiveMediaPeriod.java 336-366, 469-500). The sound also drops about 1 s, not just the picture.
(2) openStream (529-533), bufferChanged/pickAgain and keepCaptions all use trackSelectionParameters.buildUpon(), which keeps setTrackTypeDisabled(VIDEO, true). Resetting the videoOff flag isn't enough: the track type must be re-enabled explicitly in openStream, and playerFor must reset videoOff for a new player.
(3) closeStream, parkPaused and stop must remove dropPicture (only openStream is mentioned).
(4) Status.video becomes null while off, which shows in any info UI that reads it.
verdicts.amendment: In openStream and playerFor, explicitly set setTrackTypeDisabled(C.TRACK_TYPE_VIDEO, false) whenever videoOff is set, then clear the flag. Remove dropPicture in closeStream, parkPaused and stop. State in the item that bringing the picture back on TS reconnects the whole stream (about 1 s of picture and sound) and lands at the live edge. Mark it as a jump with startJump. Keep the frames-moved-within-10 s gate, because disabling flushes the codec before releasing it.

Drop the TIE change; existing behaviour and tests already cover it. Bring mv-polish item 1 into this item as a must. Track new pictures separately from movingNow, keep them INVISIBLE until the move ends, and settle them in moveEnd, in finishMotion and on the next place(). Otherwise a suspend during the move leaves them INVISIBLE after resume(), which never calls relayout. Correct the 4->3 wording and the inset figures.

verdicts.issues: The drawDoubleRoundRect API is fine: API 29+, and outer bounds equal to inner bounds pass Skia's inclusive contains check. The diagnosis is not shown, though. On Android 11 HWUI caps Skia's resource cache at width x height x 4 x 12, about 99.5 MB at 1920x1080 (CacheManager SURFACE_SIZE_MULTIPLIER 12*4). So scratch path-mask textures can't account for GL growth from 178 to 275-364 MB. Most of the growth sits outside the cache this fix and GraphicsTrim address. Also, moveEnd is 329-337, not 318-325.
verdicts.amendment: Treat fix 1 as an experiment. A/B it on the Max first: 10 large-picture toggles, recording dumpsys gfxinfo 'Total GPU memory' and 'Scratch' against meminfo GL mtrack, with the Path and then with drawDoubleRoundRect, before claiming the 14 MB per change. If GL mtrack still grows with exact corners, look for the cause elsewhere (SurfaceView resizes, the layers made during moves) before shipping fix 2 as the remedy.

verdicts.issues:
(1) PlayerHost.CANT_DECODE (PlayerHost.kt:866-871) is DECODER_INIT_FAILED, DECODER_QUERY_FAILED, DECODING_FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED and DECODING_FORMAT_EXCEEDS_CAPABILITIES. It does not include DECODING_FAILED. Tonight's decoder error was 'Live recovery: ERROR_CODE_DECODING_FAILED; try 2 in 2000 ms' (20:40:55), so 'decoder = e.errorCode in CANT_DECODE' would not fire for the case it was written for.
(2) Reconnecting at 50 ms risks a 4xx while a one-connection provider is still freeing the slot. LiveRefusal's first wait is then 1000 ms, worse than today's 300 ms; this is an assumption, not measured.
verdicts.amendment: Define decoder = errorCode in CANT_DECODE + ERROR_CODE_DECODING_FAILED (or a new DECODER_ERRORS set), and keep the give-up rule on CANT_DECODE. Ship 50 ms only after the Max log shows no 4xx after a provider close at 50 ms; otherwise use about 150 ms.

verdicts.issues:
Feasible as far as the code shows. ProgressiveMediaPeriod.onLoadCompleted sets durationUs, calls onSourceInfoRefreshed and reports DATA_TYPE_MEDIA (iconst_1 in the 1.8.0 bytecode), so the DATA_TYPE_MEDIA filter works. A prepare error of the queued period only surfaces after the renderers have read the current stream to its end, which the existing reconnect then handles. Gaps:
(1) If the next connection isn't ready in time, the BUFFERING after READY is counted as a stall: noteStall raises cushion.stalls, which raises the wait needed after later stalls, and logs a 'Live rebuffer'.
(2) Every transition fires onTracksChanged with new Tracks, which re-runs keepCaptions/pickAgain.
(3) The decoder is kept without a flush only if the new connection's SPS/PPS are identical. A mismatch on a non-adaptive MTK codec flushes it anyway.
verdicts.amendment: Mark the transition as a jump (startJump on onMediaItemTransition AUTO, or once the next item is queued) so a short wait isn't counted as a stall. Note that onTracksChanged runs again and must leave the chosen sound and captions as they are. In the Max test, add a check for any 'Flushing' or codec re-init at the transition.

verdicts.issues: LiveRefusal.shown is 'code != 0' and message() embeds the code (LiveRefusal.kt:22, 57). PlayerHost also logs refusal.code (line 692). A refusal with no HTTP code needs its own flag, or shown, message and the log all break. UnrecognizedInputFormatException is the confirmed cause (the evidence log at 20:33:28).
verdicts.amendment: Add a 'notAStream' state to LiveRefusal that counts toward the streak and makes shown true without a code. message() returns the new text in that state. PlayerHost's 'refused (code) plays' log must handle no code.

verdicts.issues: onEvents publishes on every batch (PlayerHost.kt:621, MultiviewPlayer.kt:209). Captions go through onCues and setCues, and Status carries no cues, so skipping batches with only CUES or METADATA is safe. status() is also called directly by LivePage (player.status().error), so caching the track lists helps there too. Currently Tracks is the same instance until the selection changes. No problem found.
It misses LiveSync.kt:185 ('$what for "${p.name}": put off part-way until nothing plays'), which also logs the playlist name. The evidence extract shows the host-style names in these lines.
verdicts.amendment: Lines 185, 223, 238, 265, 272, 314 and 327, and grep again for any other p.name in Log calls.

verdicts.issues: Feasible. Audio samples are all sync samples, so re-enabling audio on TS can seek inside the kept queue without a reconnect (unlike video). The plan already gates it on a Max measurement.

Item 1 is needed by the new 3->4 move (see mv-layout) and has edge cases the plan misses. moveEnd only settles movingNow. finishMotion (393-399), which suspend() calls, would leave a held-back new picture INVISIBLE, and resume() never calls relayout, so the picture stays blank. Items 2 and 3 are fine.
verdicts.amendment: Move item 1 into mv-layout as a must, with explicit settling in moveEnd, finishMotion and the next place(). Keep items 2 and 3 as 'could'.

verdicts.issues: Wrong path: ScopeLists is app/src/main/java/app/fireplayer/live/ScopeLists.kt, not live/ui/. listFor (LivePage ~1084) builds AllPlaylists as a flatMap of the per-playlist lists, so subList views need each playlist's start and end stored with the big list. Otherwise feasible.
verdicts.amendment: Fix the path. Keep each playlist's start and end offsets next to the 'All playlists' list in ScopeLists, so it is invalidated with it.

verdicts.issues:
(1) Pruning zap_group to the 'oldest' 200 keys is impossible with the current storage: they are separate 'zap_group:<key>' entries (LivePage 2648-2653) with no time or order. It needs a stored order, which is a new preference and contradicts 'no new preferences'.
(2) The duplicate-guide claim isn't supported. The two 12.9 MB guide downloads were in separate update runs, 20:33:58 and 21:04:17, after a playlist was added. Reuse within one run would have saved nothing tonight.
(3) Parking a seekable live window after 30 min changes a behaviour PausedRoom.liveSuspends documents as intended: a window that can be wound back keeps its place.
verdicts.amendment: Drop zap_group pruning, or prune without an order (for example only keys whose channel no longer exists). Restate (1) of LiveSync as 'within one run, if two playlists share a guide address' with no claimed saving from tonight. Make the 30-min seekable parking an open question.

verdicts.issues: stallCheck runs every 4 s (CHECK_MS), so 'stalled 10 s' can only be judged at 12 s, the same moment as LIMIT_MS. A reconnect throws away the 3-6 s already refilled and needs the full cushion again. If the feed really arrives slower than real time, the new connection may be no faster. The benefit is unproven and it adds reconnects (and provider connection churn, three at once in Multiview).
verdicts.amendment: Measure first. Log refill rate per stall and how fast a fresh connection fills on the same channel. Ship only if fresh connections fill clearly faster, and then for the single player only.

verdicts.issues: Measurement only. Fine.

missing: Multiview board keepScreenOn (Multiview.kt enterWith/resume set it true) is not cleared when every picture shows an error or the decoder message, so the screen never sleeps.

No plan for ERROR_CODE_TIMEOUT from surfaceDestroyed or attach on a healthy decoder (now more likely with the 500 ms cap): it must not set the global stuck state by itself. Add a Max test of the Home key and zapping during a codec start.

DecoderHealth is lost when the process restarts after an ANR (tonight pid 8778). Live TV's automatic resume then builds a player on the wedged decoder again. Say so, and check on the Max that exactly one blocked player results, with the message.

While the decoder is stuck (player == null, session PLAYING), PlayerHost.togglePause and goLive return early (player ?: return). Say what Play/OK does then: one retry, via streamDead() and Status.error.

Pure unit tests for the decisions now buried in glue code: which ERROR_CODE_TIMEOUT source counts as stuck vs suspect, the one-viewer-build-per-episode limit, and clearing stuck only on a decoder made after the mark.
Check the user's 'Multiview with 3 or 4' setting on the Max (multiview_large, default false). If it is 'One large on top', adding a 3rd picture never shows the new centred layout.
critiques.layout_issues:
The grid spec matches the request exactly. 3 pictures: two on top at 464x261 dp, the third centred underneath at (248, 273), and a half-size 16:9 'Add a channel' (232x130.5 dp) to its right, vertically centred on it. 4 pictures: the plain 2x2 grid. The gap goes 8 -> 6 dp and the radius 12 -> 8 dp. I re-derived every number. Problems:
(1) The current screenshot (mv_3tiles_now.png) is the 'One large on top' mode. That mode has the most unused space (side bands of 344-352 px around the large picture and 333 px around the bottom row), and it gets only the gap change. The user explicitly asked to use more free space, so the plan should recommend option B or C, not just leave it open. In that mode there is still no Add button.
(2) On 3->4, the centred bottom picture slides through the spot where the new 4th picture's surface already shows. The fix (keep new pictures hidden until the move ends) must be part of this must item, including finishMotion and resume.
(3) The D-pad TIE tolerance is unnecessary: the strict '<' and the existing test already send ties to the earlier stop.
