findings.summary:
I read the single-view live engine in full: playback/PlayerHost.kt, LiveSession (+ConnectionBudget), LiveLoadControl (+LiveCushion, LiveStallWatch), LiveReconnect, LiveRefusal, LiveTiming, LiveRoom, LivePause and TrackMatch. I also read the live factory (player/PlayerFactory.kt buildLive, LiveRenderersFactory, LiveDelayRenderersFactory, OffsetRenderer), LiveBuffer, PausedRoom, FilmRoom, the call sites in HomeActivity and LivePage, SyncGuard's let-go and come-back, live/SmartPlayOrchestrator.kt (unused, and not part of live TV) and the 9 pure unit-test files under app/src/test/java/app/fireplayer/playback. Repo root: /home/user/firestick-player. I confirmed Media3 1.8.0 internals with javap against the cached runtime jar.

**What actually happened tonight.** I found the real start of the incident in the scrubbed log. At 20:51:50.584 the MediaTek video daemon VPUD (pid 606) crashed with a segmentation fault. It had been logging damaged H.264 from that channel for about a minute ("H264_decode invalid NALU 2", "un-support type of NAL (25/30/4)"). The app got no error at all. Video output stopped at 20:51:49 while sound went on until the provider ended the stream at 20:52:17 (audio EOS). Media3 then sat in the READY state, reporting playing, with a frozen picture. FirePlayer logged nothing for 12 min 15 s. Nothing in the live engine watches whether the decoder is still producing frames.

**What the incident exposed:**
- **Frozen picture never noticed.** No check that video frames are still coming out of the decoder.
- **No first-picture watchdog.** The stall watch only arms after READY→BUFFERING (PlayerHost.kt:747). The first open and every reconnect go unwatched, so a stuck decoder creation spun for 92 s, and again after the app restarted.
- **2.5-second main-thread freezes and the ANR.** closeStream (547-549), playerFor (579-581) and MultiviewPlayer.releasePlayer (185-187) clear the surface before releasing. With the playback thread blocked, that costs Media3's 2000 ms detach timeout plus its 500 ms release timeout each time. That matches the 151/152/156 skipped frames. Closing two multiview tiles took 5 s, which triggered the ANR.
- **ERROR_CODE_TIMEOUT handled as a network error.** It sends the player to retry on the same dead player, and it can leave a stray retry that fires on the next channel's player.
- **Release failures are silent.** The listener is removed before release(), so the engine never learns the release failed. Each new player built on the wedged decoder then leaks its playback thread, its loader thread and its socket. Media3 reads up to 1 MiB, then waits on the blocked playback thread, which matches the ~1.3 MB left unread on each socket.

**The two agreed changes.**
1. Decoder off screen. The decoder is held while the picture is out of sight in three places: the Home/Search picture-in-picture (PiP) when covered or scrolled away (no limit, sound on, still decoding), a hidden surface (Media3 keeps decoding into a placeholder surface), and pause (10 min for plain streams, forever for HLS/DASH windows). Disabling the video track after about 60 s out of sight frees the hardware decoder and its output buffers while the sound plays on.
2. First-picture watchdog. It belongs right after p.prepare() in openStream (PlayerHost.kt:538-540) and after every reconnect or jump. It should judge by the decoder's output counters, because onRenderedFirstFrame doesn't fire while the surface is hidden. At 15 s it shows the plain "video decoder isn't responding, restart the Fire TV" message and stops building players.

**The stream that "ends".** It ended 31 times, every ~27 s (median). Each time the viewer saw a frozen last frame and silence for ~0.93 s (748-1136 ms), with a spinner after 300 ms. The content then jumped by -6.7 to +10.4 s. Two fixes: cut ENDED_FIRST_MS (300 ms) for a quick win, or append a second copy of the same channel when the provider closes the connection, so Media3 opens the new connection while the 1.5-3 s already loaded plays out. That removes the freeze and spinner; the server-side jumps stay. It needs a test on the Max.

Smaller items: the live player never waits on DecoderCheck, although films do; status is rebuilt and sent on every Media3 event batch; and channels whose stream Media3 can't read at all ("container unsupported") show "Reconnecting…" forever. All fixes I propose are cheap timers armed only while playing or opening, plus pure, testable rule classes. They add no per-frame work, no background jobs and no storage changes.

problems.title: A decoder that dies mid-play is never noticed (frozen picture, no recovery)
problems.detail: After the video daemon crash the hardware decoder stopped producing frames without reporting an error. Media3 stays READY with isPlaying true, because the video renderer counts as ready once its source has finished loading and never ends. No ENDED, no BUFFERING, no error, so none of PlayerHost's recovery paths (ENDED reconnect, stall watch, onPlayerError) ever fire. The viewer had a still picture (silent after the provider's EOS) for 12 min 15 s, and the decoder instance was held the whole time.
problems.evidence: VPUD '20:51:50.584 receive 11(Segmentation fault)'; last video bitrate line 20:51:49.629; audio EOS 20:52:17.269; no FirePlayerLive line 20:50:36 -> 21:04:05; PlayerHost.kt:683-697 (only isPlaying transitions are watched), 740-772 (stall watch needs a BUFFERING transition)
problems.fix_idea: Add a 'picture moving' check. A main-thread Runnable every 3 s, armed only while isPlaying with a video track enabled; arm in onIsPlayingChanged(true) at PlayerHost.kt:689, clear on false and in closeStream at 543-570. It reads p.videoDecoderCounters: renderedOutputBufferCount + skippedOutputBufferCount + droppedBufferCount (skipped counts while the surface is hidden, because Media3 then decodes into its placeholder). It also reads a ThreadBeat(p.playbackLooper) from player/ThreadBeat.kt. If there has been no new decoder output for ~8 s while playing, or the playback thread has been silent for >3 s: log 'Live recovery: the picture stopped (no frames for N s; sound playing/ended)', abandon the player (see the main-thread-freeze item) and open the same source once on a new player. If that one shows no picture within 15 s, the first-picture watchdog's message follows. Put the rule in a pure class (e.g. playback/LivePictureWatch.kt, modelled on player/PictureWatch.kt) with unit tests.
problems.impact: High: turns a silent 12-minute freeze into a recovery within ~10 s, or a clear message.
problems.effort: M (pure rule + tests + ~40 lines in PlayerHost)
problems.risk: Low-medium: channels with very sparse frames, or a paused or hidden picture, must not trip it. Gate on isPlaying and count skipped/dropped frames. Watch for false positives on the Max.

problems.title: First open (and every reconnect) with no picture spins forever: agreed change 2
problems.detail: openStream sets jumping=true and the stall watch only arms on READY->BUFFERING, so an open whose decoder creation hangs stays in BUFFERING with the spinner forever. The same goes for every retry. The live player also never consults DecoderCheck (films do), so a decoder service stuck at boot spins live forever too. onRenderedFirstFrame is not a usable 'picture arrived' signal on its own: it doesn't fire while the surface is hidden (placeholder surface).
problems.evidence: PlayerHost.kt:527, 612, 747; player c674fc5 Init 21:04:17.580, then only 'Surface doesn't have any previously queued frames' (21:05:42-43) until the user left at 21:05:49 (92 s); after the app restart, pid 8778 Init 21:06:59.631 -> 'IOmx service obtained' 21:07:05.122 and nothing more; PlayerActivity.kt:1216-1226 (films gate on DecoderCheck)
problems.fix_idea: (1) Add a 'firstPicture' Runnable: posted at the end of openStream right after p.prepare()/playWhenReady (PlayerHost.kt:538-540), and re-armed wherever a jump starts (retry 612-617, behind-live-window 652-654, goLive seek 372-374). Best is a startJump() helper that also sets jumping=true. Cancel it on the first decoder output (counters > 0), and in closeStream, parkPaused, when error or refusal is shown, and while the video track is deliberately disabled (agreed change 1). (2) At 15 s: if !DecoderCheck.answered, use the films' 'Fire TV's video decoder is stuck…' wording; else if the tracks are known with a video track (onTracksChanged) but onVideoDecoderInitialized never came, or it came and 0 frames were output, the decoder isn't responding. Set a new Status field (e.g. stuck = "The TV's video decoder isn't responding\nRestarting the Fire TV should fix it"), cancel the retry, build no further players, log 'Live: no picture 15 s after opening (tracks at X ms, decoder started: no); the TV's video decoder isn't responding'. If no tracks yet (the server hasn't sent anything), it is not the decoder: leave Media3's network errors and 'Reconnecting…' to handle it. (3) Show it like `refused`: HomeActivity.showBusy (1478-1487) with text at once and no spinner (BusySigns.kt:36 already supports this); PiP pages through the pipErrorSaid notice (1462-1466); keepScreenOn off (1456). (4) Call DecoderCheck.ask() on the first live open (or warm()). No storage changes; one Runnable per open.
problems.impact: High: the user's agreed change. Ends endless spinners and stops leaking a player per attempt.
problems.risk: Low: 15 s is well above the slowest measured start (4.2 s). Radio-only channels (no video track) and paused opens must be skipped.

problems.title: Main thread frozen 2.5 s per player close on a dead playback thread (the ANR)
problems.detail: closeStream and playerFor call clearVideoSurfaceView before release(), and MultiviewPlayer.releasePlayer does the same. With the playback thread blocked, each close waits Media3's full 2000 ms detach timeout, then the 500 ms release timeout. Hiding the surface (surfaceDestroyed) also waits up to 2 s. Opening Multiview (single player stopped) froze the UI 2.56 s; closing it with 2 stuck tiles took 5 s, and Fire OS raised an ANR and killed the app.
problems.evidence: PlayerHost.kt:547-549, 579-581; MultiviewPlayer.kt:185-187; PlayerFactory.kt:324-332 (no timeouts set); '21:05:49.648 ERROR_CODE_TIMEOUT' -> '21:05:50.156 Skipped 151 frames', 'Davey! duration=2574ms'; '21:06:23.831 ERROR_CODE_TIMEOUT' -> '21:06:24.374 Skipped 152 frames', 'Davey 2560ms'; multiview tiles '21:06:33.948' and '21:06:36.451 a picture's ERROR_CODE_TIMEOUT' -> 'Multiview: closed 21:06:36.954' -> signal 3 at 21:06:37.634 -> 'ANR ... Waited 5000ms for KeyEvent'
problems.fix_idea: (1) In buildLive (PlayerFactory.kt:324-332) add .setDetachSurfaceTimeoutMs(500); keep the 500 ms release timeout. This covers single view and Multiview at once. (2) Before releasing, check a ThreadBeat for that player: if its thread has been silent >1 s, skip clearVideoSurfaceView and go straight to release(), so the main thread waits at most 0.5 s. (3) Always removeListener first, then clear, then release, so a timeout error raised during the close doesn't trigger recovery. (4) Time the release: SystemClock.uptimeMillis() around p.release(); if it took >= ~450 ms, set a process-wide 'decoderTrouble' flag and log 'Live: the player took N ms to let go; its decoder may be stuck'. The watchdogs above use that flag to say so sooner and to build no more players.
problems.impact: High: removes the 2.5 s freezes and the ANR.
problems.risk: Low: on a healthy device the surface detach finishes in a few ms; 500 ms still covers a busy thread.

problems.title: ERROR_CODE_TIMEOUT treated as a network failure; stray retry hits the next player
problems.detail: An ERROR_CODE_TIMEOUT means the player's own thread didn't answer, but onPlayerError sends it to the generic reconnect, and retry() re-prepares the same blocked player, which spins forever. In closeStream, removeCallbacks(retry) runs BEFORE clearVideoSurfaceView, so the timeout error raised by the clear posts a fresh retry that survives the close (harmless only because player==null). In playerFor, openStream has already removed retry (503) before the old player is cleared (579). The old player's error then posts a retry that fires 1 s later on the NEW channel's player: p.stop() mid-open at 614, and reconnecting=true shown for a channel that never failed.
problems.evidence: PlayerHost.kt:503, 508, 521, 544 vs 547, 579-580, 604-618, 657-680; log pairs 'Live recovery: ERROR_CODE_TIMEOUT; try 1 in 1000 ms' immediately followed by 'ExoPlayerImpl Release' (21:05:49.648/.649, 21:06:23.831/.832)
problems.fix_idea: In onPlayerError (647), handle PlaybackException.ERROR_CODE_TIMEOUT separately: log 'the player's thread isn't answering', abandon the player (no clear, release once), mark decoderTrouble, and open the source once on a new player under the first-picture watchdog. Never retry it on the same player. Move removeListener before any clear in closeStream (547-548) and playerFor (579-580), and call main.removeCallbacks(retry) after release() as well.
problems.impact: Medium-high: no infinite spinner after a timeout, no phantom reconnect on the next channel.
problems.risk: Low

problems.title: Each player built on a stuck decoder leaks its threads, socket and buffer
problems.detail: When codec creation blocks inside the OMX service, release() times out and the playback thread never finishes. Its loader thread waits after reading ~1 MiB, the HTTP socket stays open with unread data and ends up in CLOSE_WAIT, and the allocator memory stays. PlayerHost keeps building new players for each resume, Multiview and channel change: 7 decoder creations stopped at 'IOmx service obtained' tonight. The app can't kill a thread blocked in native code, so the only defences are not to build more players and to cut the network side.
problems.evidence: 'OMXClient IOmx service obtained' at 21:04:18, 21:05:55, 21:06:05, 21:06:26, 21:06:27, 21:06:41, 21:07:05 (makeComponentInstance only for the first); task facts: ~1.3 MB unread per channel socket, 3 sockets in CLOSE_WAIT; ProgressiveMediaSource.DEFAULT_LOADING_CHECK_INTERVAL_BYTES = 1048576
problems.fix_idea: (1) Once decoderTrouble is set (slow release, thread silent, or the 15 s watchdog), build no automatic players: the message stands, and a channel change or OK tries once more. (2) Add a small 'connection kill switch' DataSource wrapper in buildLive, modelled on player/IdleCloseDataSource.kt: it registers each open upstream for its player, and PlayerHost.abandon(p) closes them on a background thread. That frees the provider connection and kernel buffers even though the thread stays stuck. (3) Optional, measure first on the Max: with the hardware decoder stuck, one try with software decoding, using a MediaCodecSelector that drops hardware video decoders. c2.android.avc runs in the separate software codec process, which kept working tonight for the sound. Check CPU at 720p/1080p before adopting, and say 'Restarting the Fire TV brings back the smooth picture'.
problems.impact: Medium: memory and connections stay bounded when the decoder is stuck; the provider's connection allowance isn't held by dead sockets.
problems.effort: M (S for 1, M for 2, M plus device testing for 3)
problems.risk: Low for 1; medium for 2 (closing from another thread must be idempotent); medium for 3 (CPU load on 1.7 GB / 4-core Stick).

problems.title: Hardware decoder held while the picture is out of sight: agreed change 1
problems.detail: The Home/Search picture covered by a title page, See all or a settings window, or scrolled off the top: the surface stays VISIBLE under the wallpaper, so every frame is decoded and rendered for as long as the page stays. A hidden surface (INVISIBLE) is decoded into Media3's placeholder surface. A paused plain stream keeps decoder, buffer and connection for 10 min; a paused live HLS/DASH window keeps them indefinitely. Disabling the video track makes Media3 disable and reset the video renderer (ExoPlayerImplInternal.enableRenderers resets renderers no longer selected), which releases the hardware decoder and its output buffers while the sound plays on.

When unseen, postDelayed(dropPicture, ~60 s); dropPicture sets p.trackSelectionParameters…setTrackTypeDisabled(C.TRACK_TYPE_VIDEO, true) and logs 'Live: picture out of sight 60 s, its video decoder let go (sound plays on)'. When seen again, remove the callback; if dropped, re-enable the track and re-arm the first-picture watchdog. A plain TS stream restarts its connection to reach a keyframe, so ~1 s with the spinner after 300 ms. The same step for a paused live window after PausedRoom.LIVE_MS. Put the rule in a pure class with tests (e.g. playback/LiveOffScreen.kt). The freeze and first-picture checks skip while the track is off. No per-frame work, no storage.
problems.impact: Medium: frees the decoder and tens of MB of decoder buffers on the 1.7 GB Stick while PiP sits covered; less decoder churn.
problems.risk: Low-medium: verify on the Max that re-enabling brings the picture back within ~1 s on TS and HLS, and that captions and audio track choices survive (they are separate track types).

problems.title: A stream that 'ends' every ~27 s freezes and spins each time; could be near-seamless
problems.detail: The provider closed the stream 31 times (13-72 s apart). PlayerHost only reacts at STATE_ENDED, after the already-loaded tail has played out, then waits 300 ms and seeks to restart, which opens a new connection. The viewer gets a frozen frame and silence for 0.75-1.14 s with the spinner after 300 ms, then a content jump. Media3 starts loading the next item as soon as the current one is fully loaded and its duration known (ProgressiveMediaPeriod sets the duration when the load completes). So a queued copy of the same channel would open the new connection when the provider closes the old one, while the 1.5-3 s tail still plays.
problems.evidence: 31 'Live recovery: stream ended; try 1 in 300 ms' 20:35:43-20:50:35; 'playing again after' avg 930 ms (748-1136); PTS jumps at reconnect -6.7..+10.4 s ('Possible seek found!'); PlayerHost.kt:713-721, 604-618; LiveReconnect.kt:62; javap MediaPeriodQueue.shouldLoadNextMediaPeriod (needs isFullyBuffered and durationUs set), ProgressiveMediaPeriod.onLoadCompleted -> onSourceInfoRefreshed
problems.fix_idea: (a) Quick win: ENDED_FIRST_MS 300 -> ~50 ms (LiveReconnect.kt:62; update LiveReconnectTest.kt:23), saving ~0.25 s per event. (b) Seamless chain, plain streams only (kind TS/'stream', not HLS/DASH): in the `bandwidth` AnalyticsListener (PlayerHost.kt:724) add onLoadCompleted for media loads and, on the main thread, if mediaItemCount == 1, call p.addMediaItem(liveMediaItem(source)). In onMediaItemTransition(reason AUTO) remove item 0 and log 'Live: the provider ended the stream (X ms loaded ahead); the next connection took over'. Guard with a pure rule: if the item that ended played < ~5 s, don't chain, so it reaches ENDED and today's back-off applies (no tight connection loop). The ConnectionBudget lease is unchanged: the old connection is already closed. The server-side content jumps remain, but no freeze, spinner, decoder flush or ENDED. Must be tried on the Max with that channel first.
problems.impact: High for viewers of such channels: ~1 s freeze every ~27 s becomes no freeze.
problems.risk: (a) low. (b) medium: Media3 playlist behaviour with unknown-duration progressive items needs device verification, and the guard must stop loops on empty or instantly closing responses.

problems.title: A decoder error waits out the back-off and shows black
problems.detail: After ERROR_CODE_DECODING_FAILED the stream itself is fine, but the retry used the shared back-off (2 s, because a stream-ended event 3 s earlier had counted try 1). The decoder was released, so the surface lost its frames (black, glass copy failing) for 2.8 s.

problems.impact: Medium: ~2 s less black after each decoder error on damaged channels.
problems.risk: Low

problems.title: Status rebuilt and sent on every Media3 event batch
problems.detail: playerListener.onEvents calls publish() for every batch, including caption changes (which already have their own onCues path), metadata and loading toggles. status() rebuilds the caption and audio track lists, with java.util.Locale display-name lookups, and notifies LivePage, HomeActivity and SyncGuard each time. Not per frame, but with captions on or HLS metadata it is several times a second for nothing new.
problems.evidence: PlayerHost.kt:621, 630, 818-854 (Locale at 850); listeners LivePage.kt:729-739, HomeActivity.kt:1450-1471, SyncGuard.kt:249-256
problems.fix_idea: In onEvents return early when the events contain only EVENT_CUES / EVENT_METADATA / EVENT_IS_LOADING_CHANGED. Alternatively, keep the last Status and skip notifying when the new one is equal (data class equality). Cache the tracksOf() results per Tracks instance.
problems.impact: Low-medium: less main-thread churn while watching with captions.
problems.risk: Low: make sure busy/reconnect signs still update (they ride on state and isPlaying events).

problems.title: 'Container unsupported' channels show 'Reconnecting…' and are retried forever
problems.detail: A channel whose response no extractor can read (the provider sends something that isn't a video stream) is retried with the network back-off for as long as the viewer stays, and shows 'Reconnecting…'. That's misleading: retrying won't fix it, and it is said in plain words for 4xx refusals but not here.

problems.impact: Low-medium: clearer, and fewer pointless requests to the provider.
problems.risk: Low

findings.summary:
Read-only review of Multiview: MultiviewRules.kt (MultiviewLayout, MultiviewRules, MultiviewModel), MultiviewBoard.kt, Multiview.kt, MultiviewPlayer.kt, MultiviewLeases.kt, their tests, how LivePage opens and closes Multiview, and the scrubbed log from the Max. Geometry was recomputed with a copy of the layout maths in <scratchpad>/mvcalc/geo.py and feat.py. The Max runs at density 2, so 1 dp = 2 px.

LAYOUT TODAY. All the maths lives in one pure object, MultiviewLayout (MultiviewRules.kt:14-123), working in dp on a 960 x 540 dp screen. One 8 dp value (MV_GAP) is both the edge margin and the gap between pictures. Every picture is 16:9.
- 2 pictures: side by side, 936x527 px at (16,277) and (968,277).
- 3 pictures (grid): 2 x 2 grid of 917x516 px cells at (35,16), (968,16), (35,548), (968,548). The 4th cell is a FULL-SIZE "Add a channel" panel.
- 4 pictures: the same grid.
- One large on top (OK on a picture, or the setting "One large on top"): large picture 1216x684 px at (352,16); small ones 619x348 px in a row at y=716, always sized as if three fit across. The screenshot shows this layout.
- Corners: 12 dp (24 px), drawn as board-black paths over each picture's corners. Nothing is clipped by an outline.
- Video fit: the surface is sized to the video's shape and fitted inside the picture, so video is never cropped. Letterboxed video ends up with square visible corners.
- Selection ring: 3 dp white, drawn outside the picture.

NEW LAYOUT. Only the pure layout code, two constants and the tests need to change. The board already places and fades the Add cell from whatever box the layout gives it.
- 3 pictures: 2 on top, 1 centred underneath, and "Add" as a half-size 16:9 button to the right of the bottom picture, vertically centred on it.
- 4 pictures: the plain 2 x 2 grid.
- Gap: 8 → 6 dp.
- Corner radius: 12 → 8 dp.
- Proposed px: 2 pictures 942x530 at (12,275) and (966,275). Grid cells 928x522 at (26,12), (966,12), (26,546), (966,546); with 3 pictures the bottom one sits at (496,546) and Add is 464x261 at (1436,677). Large picture 1232x693 with small ones 624x351.

The grid is already at about 96% of the largest possible 16:9 cell, so bigger pictures in the grid can only come from smaller gaps. The large black side bands in the one-large layout are a design question for the user; two options with numbers are below.

OPTIMISATION FINDINGS.
1. Tonight's slow open and the freeze on closing were teardown waits on the main thread, not Multiview's own work. A healthy open (20:34:49) took about 210 ms and logged no skipped frames.
   - Each player teardown calls clearVideoSurfaceView before release(). On a stuck decoder, Media3 waits 2000 ms for the surface to detach and then reports ERROR_CODE_TIMEOUT, and release() then waits another 500 ms.
   - Opening tonight: PlayerHost.stop() inside enterMultiview took 2.5 s. That is the Davey 2560 ms and the 152 skipped frames.
   - Closing tonight: 2 pictures x 2.5 s = 5.0 s with the main thread frozen, which led to the ANR. 4 pictures would freeze it for 10 s.
   - The "Multiview recovery: a picture's ERROR_CODE_TIMEOUT" lines were this teardown, not a real recovery. The listener was still attached, and it left a stray retry behind.
   - release() already removes the surface callbacks itself (checked in the Media3 1.8.0 bytecode). Dropping the clear step and removing the listener first cuts each stuck teardown to 0.5 s.
2. A picture has no first-frame watchdog. The stall watch only starts after the picture has played once, so a stuck first open shows a spinner with no text, forever (agreed change 2 is needed here too). Tonight both pictures reached "IOmx service obtained" and never got a decoder.
3. Each picture holds one hardware decoder and one software AAC decoder; muted pictures still decode their sound.
4. The max-video limits only help streams that offer several sizes. A 1080p TS channel in a 1280x720-limited picture still opened a 1920x1080 decoder.
5. On top of the buffer, each picture holds a hardware decoder's video buffers (estimated, not measured). Two pictures already pushed Fire OS to its critical memory level within 6 s.
6. The FFmpeg video decoder is loaded after the hardware decoder in every player. Its library includes h264, hevc and mpeg2video, and decoder fallback is on. Whether a 4th picture could silently fall back to software decoding needs checking on the Max.

problems.title: Closing or opening Multiview on a stuck decoder freezes the main thread 2.5 s per player (5 s with 2 pictures led to tonight's ANR)
problems.detail: MultiviewPlayer.releasePlayer calls clearVideoSurfaceView before removeListener and release. On a stuck playback thread, Media3 blocks for the 2000 ms detach timeout, raises ERROR_CODE_TIMEOUT to the still-attached listener (the fake 'Multiview recovery' line plus a stray retry posted after removeCallbacks), and release() then blocks another 500 ms. dropTile, suspend, closeAll and Change channel with other headers all go through this path. With 4 pictures a close would freeze the main thread for 10 s. PlayerHost.closeStream has the identical pattern, which caused the 2.5 s freeze at Multiview open. The stray retry can also hit a NEW player: open() resets the retry state, and only then does playerFor() release the old player.
problems.evidence: MultiviewPlayer.kt:181-188, :120 (attach also clears), :83-95 (reset happens before playerFor), :86 vs :182; PlayerHost.kt:543-550; log 21:06:33.948 / 21:06:36.451 / 21:06:36.954 and 21:06:23.831 -> 21:06:24.345; ANR at 21:06:52.415
problems.fix_idea:
In releasePlayer (and PlayerHost.closeStream):
- remove the listener first;
- do not call clearVideoSurfaceView before release(). release() itself removes the surface callbacks and releases the codec (checked in the Media3 1.8.0 bytecode).
- keep the default 500 ms release timeout. Healthy releases take about 50 ms (log 20:35:01.690 -> .738).
In attach(), skip the clear when no player exists. Optional: release the stuck picture first once the watchdog has flagged it, so the healthy ones are not waiting behind it.
problems.impact: Stuck-decoder close: 5.0 s -> 1.0 s for 2 pictures and 10 s -> 2 s for 4, which removes the ANR path. Multiview open on a stuck decoder: 2.5 s -> 0.5 s. No more fake recovery lines or stray retries.
problems.effort: Small: about 6 lines per player class.
problems.risk: Low. Healthy behaviour is the same, because release() already detaches the surface. A picture's SurfaceView is reused by the next picture only after release() returns.

problems.title: A picture whose decoder never starts spins forever (agreed change 2 must cover Multiview too)
problems.detail: The stall watch starts only after READY, and the busy signs show a spinner with no words while not reconnecting. When creating the decoder hangs inside Fire OS (tonight: 'IOmx service obtained', never makeComponentInstance), the picture just spins. Its socket fills up and stays unread, since the buffer stops at 10 s. Opening more pictures in that state piles up more stuck threads.
problems.evidence: MultiviewPlayer.kt:261-277, :266; BusySigns.kt:35-36; log 21:06:26.702 and 21:06:27.109; incident notes: 1.3 MB unread per socket, sockets in CLOSE_WAIT
problems.fix_idea: Use the same pure first-picture rule as PlayerHost (shared helper). Arm it in open(); cancel it in onRenderedFirstFrame (one listener override). After ~15 s with tracks known (data arrived) and no 'video decoder initialised' callback: release the player (cheap after the teardown fix), set error = a plain line such as "This TV's video decoder isn't responding. Restarting the Fire TV should fix it", and set a process-wide 'decoder not responding' flag. While that flag is set, addPicture and Change channel refuse with the same notice instead of building another player. With no data yet (network), leave the normal retry logic alone, but show waiting words after a while. Add one log line per picture on its first frame (a 'Multiview: a picture shown in N ms (decoder M ms)' counterpart of LiveTiming), so open times can be measured.
problems.impact: No endless spinners. Stops the stuck-decoder pile-up that ended in tonight's ANR and restart.
problems.effort: Small-medium: about 40 lines plus a pure-rule test.
problems.risk: Low with the 'tracks known' condition. Without it, a slow server could be wrongly blamed on the decoder.

problems.title: ERROR_CODE_TIMEOUT from a picture is retried like a network failure

problems.evidence: MultiviewPlayer.kt:231-239 (falls through to reconnectAfter for every non-decode error)
problems.fix_idea: In onPlayerError, treat ERROR_CODE_TIMEOUT like the stuck-decoder case above: release once, show the plain message, set the shared flag.
problems.impact: Fewer pointless retries on a broken decoder.
problems.risk: Low.

problems.title: Possible silent software decoding in a picture (needs checking on the Max)
problems.detail: Every picture's player loads the FFmpeg video renderer (h264/hevc/mpeg2video) after the hardware one, with decoder fallback on. If the hardware decoder instances run out at the 4th picture, fallback to a software decoder, or a format the hardware rejects, could decode a 1080p picture in software. That would load the CPU and stutter the interface instead of showing 'This TV can't play another picture at once'.
problems.evidence: PlayerFactory.kt:321-323; log 'Loaded FfmpegVideoRenderer.' per player; no software video decoder seen in tonight's log (grep count 0)

problems.risk: Low.

problems.title: Silent pictures still decode sound

problems.impact: Small.
problems.risk: Medium (audible or visible hiccup on moving the selection).

problems.title: Retries are not staggered, and a stream that 'ends' regularly loops forever (shared with the live player)
problems.detail: All pictures dropped at the same moment (a network blip) reconnect together with the same quick waits. A stream that ends about every 20 s resets the retry count after 10 s of steady play, so it does 300 ms reconnects forever. Tonight the full-screen live player did this 31 times. problems.impact: Fewer simultaneous reconnect bursts and less decoder churn.
problems.risk: Low.

findings.summary:
I did a read-only review of the Live TV page and UI lifecycle (LivePage, HomeActivity's live picture and PiP, PlayerHost, Multiview and MultiviewPlayer, BusyOverlay and BusySigns, PipRules, and the guide and search code), checked against tonight's Max log. The scrubbed copy I made is at <scratchpad>/lifecycle_safe.txt. No code was edited.

The biggest finding changes the diagnosis. The decoder that sat idle from 20:51 to 21:04 was not held by a UI state. At 20:51:50 the MediaTek video service (vendor vpud) crashed with SIGSEGV in libvcodecdrv.so H264_decode. Before that it had logged 40-90 "H264_decode invalid NALU" / "un-support type of NAL" errors a minute since 20:34, on the channel whose stream ended every ~20 s. Video output stopped at 20:51:49 and the sound ran on until 20:52:17 (EOS). The player stayed READY and "playing", so PlayerHost saw no event at all. It has no stall watch, no reconnect and no message for this case. FirePlayer logged nothing from 20:50:36 to 21:04:10. keepScreenOn stayed on, so the TV showed a frozen picture for 12 minutes.

The hangs and the ANR came from Media3 calls on the main thread against a wedged playback thread:
- Every close calls clearVideoSurfaceView, which blocks for the default 2000 ms surface-detach timeout, then release(), which blocks for the default 500 ms.
- That is 2.5 s per player. It matches "spent 2534ms processing KeyEvent" (21:05:50), Davey 2560 ms on Multiview open (21:06:24), and 5111 ms on Multiview close with 2 tiles (21:06:37), which caused the ANR.

After the wedge, FirePlayer built 6 more players on its own (update comeback, tab returns, relaunch, 2 Multiview tiles, back to full screen). Each one hung creating its codec and leaked a thread and a socket.

The UI lifecycle itself is sound. The guide preview and full screen share one player and one surface. Leaving for Movies, TV Shows, My List or Settings, onStop, a film starting, an update and Multiview all release the player. The only places where a decoder keeps running with no picture on screen are:
- Home/Search PiP while it is covered (title page, See all, settings window) or scrolled out of sight. It plays on under the wallpaper with sound, with no time limit.
- PiP with no place to show it (placeVideo(null) hides the surface while decoding goes on).
- A paused channel: up to 10 min for TS, with no limit for a seekable window.

Where the two agreed changes go:
- (1) The off-screen signal belongs in HomeActivity. It is the only code that knows whether the surface is visible (settleVideo, hideVideo, showPipShift, showPipSizing, showPipHole, setMultiview). The timer and the action belong in PlayerHost. The action is to turn the video track off, which frees the codec while the sound and connection stay (I checked that Media3 resets a disabled renderer). The picture comes back when shown again.
- (2) The 15 s timer belongs in PlayerHost: armed in openStream, in retry and when video comes back; cancelled in onRenderedFirstFrame. The message belongs in a new Status field, shown by HomeActivity.showBusy in the BusyOverlay as fixed text without the spinner, where "Reconnecting…" and the refusal line appear today. Multiview tiles show it through MultiviewBoard.setMessage, and PiP pages say it once. It should also cover a picture that freezes mid-stream (frame counter not moving for 15 s), which is what actually happened tonight. After it shows, automatic retries and new players should stop.

Channel change speed is network-bound, not UI-bound: key to stream request takes 0-87 ms, and the rest (tracks at 639-3133 ms) is the provider. The main costs that would grow with more playlists:
- With 2 or more big playlists, the kept lists push each other out (one big list is kept).
- The guide builds its index on the main thread, and looks up rows one by one.
- Each Channel object carries its stream link.

Database reads are all off the main thread.

facts.claim: The 12-minute 'idle decoder' (20:51:55-21:04:05) began with a crash of the MediaTek video service, not with any UI state that held a decoder off screen.
facts.evidence: lifecycle_safe.txt: '20:51:50.636 F/libc (606): Fatal signal 11 (SIGSEGV) ... in tid 622 (vdec_srv), pid 606 (vpud)'; backtrace '#00 pc 000b427c /vendor/lib/libvcodecdrv.so (H264_decode+1212)'; '20:51:50.821 Tombstone written'; '20:51:50.892 I/VPUD (6816): vpud without fuse' (restarted as a new pid). The first 'GetCmd() line: 453 No command in 5 seconds' is at 20:51:55.612, 146 lines in all, the last at 21:04:00.650.

facts.claim: The stream fed the decoder a damaged H.264 bitstream for the whole session before the crash.
facts.evidence: VPUD '[Err] H264_decode invalid NALU 2!!' and '? un-support type of NAL (n)' lines per minute: 20:34 26, 20:35 71, 20:36 44 ... 20:50 45, 20:51 89. There was also an earlier decoder fatal error at 20:40:55 ('MtkOmxVdecExV4L2 set mFATALError', 'Live recovery: ERROR_CODE_DECODING_FAILED; try 2'), recovered in 2790 ms.

facts.claim: After the crash, video stopped at once while the sound played on for 27 s. FirePlayer then logged nothing at all for 13 minutes: no stall, no reconnect, no message.
facts.evidence: The last 'HW.omx.video.avc.bitrateInKbps' line is at 20:51:49.629. 'SW.c2.audio.mp4a.bitrateInKbps' continues to 20:52:15, then '20:52:17.269 updatePTSTime [SW.c2.audio.mp4a] EOS pts:0'. There is no FirePlayerLive line between '20:50:36.217 Live recovery: playing again after 886 ms' and '21:04:10.951 Playlist ...: lists'.

facts.claim: PlayerHost only watches stalls that go from READY to BUFFERING. A player stuck in READY with a dead video codec, or one that never leaves BUFFERING on its first open, is never checked.
facts.evidence: PlayerHost.kt:747 'Player.STATE_BUFFERING -> if (was == Player.STATE_READY && !jumping ...)' arms stallCheck. stallCheck (PlayerHost.kt:785-797) returns unless the state is BUFFERING. Nothing watches rendered frames.

facts.claim: During the freeze the TV was kept awake on a frozen picture, because the status said it was playing.
facts.evidence: HomeActivity.kt:1456-1457: keepScreenOn = status.key != null && error == null && !paused && waiting == null && refused == null. All of these held during 20:52-21:04.

facts.claim: The player was released at 21:04:05 by the update for the newly added third playlist (SyncGuard let go of the playing channel), and that release is what wedged the decoder process.
facts.evidence: '21:04:05.302 MediaCodec ... setting surface generation' (clearVideoSurfaceView), '21:04:05.314 ExoPlayerImpl Release 46c6b39', '21:04:05.830 Skipped 34 frames' (the 500 ms release wait), then '21:04:08.345 ACodec signalError(omxError 0x80001001, internalError -110)', 'Disable failed', 'Reset failed', 'sending message to a Handler on a dead thread', 'FlushInputPort() WAIT timeout(5 s)', 'failed to enter Idle state'. The download follows at '21:04:10.951 Playlist ...: lists 2996 KB in 2444 ms' after SyncPlan.SETTLE_MS = 1500 (SyncGuard.kt:134-160), and '21:04:17.580 ExoPlayerImpl Init c674fc5' comes right after 'EPG ... in 4558 ms' (backAfterUpdate). Playlists went from 2 (137 groups, 20:33:27) to 3 (261 groups, 21:05:52).

facts.claim: The typing at 21:03-21:04 was text sent from the phone's Fire TV Remote app into a FirePlayer text field (most likely the Add playlist form, not Live TV search). problems.title: A picture that freezes mid-stream after a decoder failure is never noticed (tonight's 12 minutes)
problems.detail: When the vendor video service crashed, the video codec stopped giving frames without any error. The player stayed READY. Once the sound ran out, the media clock moved to the standalone clock, so the position kept moving too. So no state change, no stall watch, no reconnect and no message; keepScreenOn stayed on. A watch on the playback position would also miss this. The signal that does catch it is the video frame counter not advancing.
problems.evidence: vpud SIGSEGV 20:51:50; last video bitrate 20:51:49; audio EOS 20:52:17; no FirePlayerLive line 20:50:36-21:04:10; PlayerHost.kt:747 and 785-797 watch only BUFFERING; HomeActivity.kt:1456.
problems.fix_idea: In PlayerHost, while status.playing and a video track is selected and wanted (not paused, picture not deliberately off), run one main-thread check every ~5 s (one handler post, nothing per frame). It reads player.videoDecoderCounters rendered + skipped + dropped. If none move for 15 s: log one line and reconnect once with a fresh player (released without the surface detach, see the next problem). If no first frame follows within 15 s, show the 'decoder isn't responding' message from change 2. Clear it on onRenderedFirstFrame.
problems.impact: Tonight the message would have shown about 15-30 s after 20:51:50 instead of a silent frozen picture for 12 minutes. The TV would also have been allowed to sleep.
problems.risk: A channel whose picture stops but whose sound goes on (radio-style feeds, still slides) could trip it. Only count channels that have shown frames, and skip tracks with no video. DecoderCounters are written on the playback thread; an approximate read is fine.
problems.effort: S-M (PlayerHost + a small pure watch class with unit tests)

problems.title: Releasing a player whose playback thread is stuck freezes the UI 2.5 s per player (ANR on Multiview close)
problems.detail: closeStream, playerFor and MultiviewPlayer.releasePlayer call clearVideoSurfaceView and then release() on the main thread. Media3 waits up to 2000 ms for the surface detach and up to 500 ms for release. With the codec wedged, each close costs 2.5 s: leaving the tab 2.53 s, opening Multiview 2.56 s, closing Multiview with 2 tiles 5.1 s, which was the ANR. onStop with N Multiview tiles has the same cost N times.
problems.evidence: PlayerHost.kt:547-549 and 579-581, MultiviewPlayer.kt:120 and 185-187; PlayerFactory.kt:324-332 (no timeout set); javap defaults 2000/500; tonight's 2534, 2560 and 5111 ms lines.
problems.fix_idea: Set ExoPlayer.Builder.setDetachSurfaceTimeoutMs(~400-500) in PlayerFactory.buildLive; a healthy detach is a few ms (setOutputSurface). Skip clearVideoSurfaceView entirely for a player flagged as stuck (watch fired, or its last release took 450 ms or more, measured with SystemClock around release()). For a stuck player, give the SurfaceView a fresh surface (visibility off and on) before the next player attaches. Release it with main.post after the transition frame so the move or close draws first. Later option: build live players on their own application looper so blocking calls never land on the UI thread.
problems.impact: Worst-case freeze per closed player drops from 2.5 s to under 1 s, and the stuck-player path skips the detach. Multiview close with 2-4 wedged tiles stays well under the 5 s ANR limit.
problems.risk: Without clearing the surface first, a healthy but slow release (over 500 ms) could leave the old codec connected when the next player attaches, failing its decoder start. That is why only stuck players skip the clear, and healthy ones keep it with the shorter timeout. Needs a TV test of channel change, Multiview in and out, and onStop.

problems.title: Change 2: a channel that shows no picture within ~15 s spins forever
problems.detail: On a first open, or a reopen after the wedge, the playback thread hangs creating the codec. The state never leaves BUFFERING, no error arrives, and BusyOverlay shows only the spinner: 'Reconnecting…' needs status.reconnecting, which never comes. Tonight: 92 s of spinner, then the viewer gave up.
problems.evidence: PlayerHost.kt:747 (stall watch only after READY); HomeActivity.kt:1478-1487 (text only when reconnecting, waiting or refused); BusyOverlay.kt:91 (no text without the spinner); 21:04:17-21:05:49 with no recovery line.
problems.fix_idea:
Timer in PlayerHost: one Runnable armed in openStream, in retry and when video comes back after change 1; cancelled in onRenderedFirstFrame, closeStream, a pause, and while video is deliberately off. At 15 s, if a video format has arrived (add onVideoInputFormatChanged to the existing analytics listener at PlayerHost.kt:724-733) but no frame: set a new Status field such as stuck = 'The TV's video decoder isn't responding\nRestarting the Fire TV may be needed', stop retry and stallCheck, and log one line. If no data arrived at all, it is the network: arm the existing stall/reconnect path from the first open, so it says 'Reconnecting…' instead of spinning. Showing it:
(a) HomeActivity.showBusy draws the text in the BusyOverlay without the spinner (BusyOverlay needs a static-text mode, since show() hides text when not spinning), centred on the picture in the miniature and full screen like the refusal line.
(b) keepScreenOn is false while stuck (HomeActivity.kt:1456).
(c) LivePage treats stuck like error: OK on the channel tries again (pick, LivePage.kt:1441); no automatic full screen (idleToFull, 2290); Play/Pause and held-Back guards (2345, 2436, 2478).
(d) PiP pages say it once, as pipErrorSaid does (HomeActivity.kt:1462-1467).
(e) Multiview tiles get the same text through MultiviewPlayer.error / MultiviewBoard.setMessage.
(f) Multiview.begin refuses with a notice while the live player is stuck.
(g) No automatic new players while stuck (onScreenStarted resume, backAfterUpdate, Multiview tiles); the viewer's own OK or channel change tries once more. Any first frame clears it.
problems.impact: The viewer gets a plain reason and next step, and FirePlayer stops piling up stuck players, threads and sockets (6 tonight).
problems.risk: It must not fire for: audio-only channels (no video track); slow servers (no format yet, so the network path applies); a refused channel or a CANT_DECODE error (those messages win); a pause during opening; video deliberately off (change 1). The text must stay within 2 lines of 13 sp in a 340 dp box (it does: 39 and 36 characters).

problems.title: Change 1: a hidden PiP keeps its video decoder running with no time limit
problems.detail: On Home and Search, while a title page, See all or the settings window covers the picture's place, or the page is scrolled past it, the channel plays on under the wallpaper with sound and a running hardware decoder, with no limit. With no place for it (pipSpot null) the surface is hidden and Media3 decodes on to a placeholder surface. None of the Live TV page's own states do this.
problems.fix_idea:
The signal belongs in HomeActivity, the only code that knows whether the surface is seen. Add one 'seen' boolean, set where the surface or hole changes: settleVideo (seen unless PiP is hidden), hideVideo (no), showPipShift / showPipSizing / showPipHole (hole null = no), setMultiview(true) (no). Call player.pictureSeen(v) only when it changes; it is a single compare in the per-frame PiP follow.
PlayerHost owns the timer: pictureSeen(false) posts one Runnable for ~60 s. When it fires, if a stream is open and not paused, turn the video track type off (Media3 then resets the video renderer and frees the codec; sound and connection stay) and log one line. pictureSeen(true) cancels the timer and turns video back on, marked as a jump so it isn't counted as a stall; the no-picture timer of change 2 re-arms. Re-apply the setting after openStream and bufferChanged while still hidden. Optional: when PiP is muted and hidden, a full suspend could stand in for this, but it costs the lease and a slower return.
problems.impact: Frees the hardware decoder and its buffers (the Max had ~197 MB free with 3 tiles) during long title-page or See all visits with a channel playing, without stopping the sound the viewer chose to keep.
problems.risk:
Must keep:
- A quick return: covers shorter than ~60 s cost nothing. After that the picture needs a keyframe, and for TS possibly a new request (~1 s); the spinner shows after 300 ms.
- PiP Full screen and held Back: turn video back on before the grow.
- PiP Volume and Close, Channel buttons on Home and Search, captions, audio delay.
- The status videoSize goes UNKNOWN while video is off: HomeActivity relays the hidden surface at 16:9, which is harmless.
- Change 2's timer must ignore deliberately-off video.
Multiview needs nothing: its pictures are always on screen and the one player is stopped there.

problems.title: A paused seekable live channel keeps its decoder with no time limit
problems.detail: parkPaused lets go of a paused channel after 10 minutes only for a plain stream. A live window that can be wound back (HLS/DASH) keeps its buffer, decoder and connection for as long as it stays paused (the picture is a still frame).
problems.evidence: PlayerHost.kt:335-347; PausedRoom.kt:106-108 (liveSuspends requires !seekable).
problems.fix_idea: Leave as it is, or also park a seekable window once it is paused beyond its live window, or after e.g. 30 min (the window will have moved past it anyway).
problems.impact: Small: only for long pauses on HLS/DASH channels.
problems.risk: The viewer's 'wind back after pause' expectation; the place is kept only while it is still inside the window.

problems.title: Leaving Multiview reopens the stream from scratch
problems.detail: Opening Multiview stops and releases the one live player (its channel is reopened by the first tile on a new connection). Leaving releases every tile and builds a new live player for the chosen channel. Each handover costs a new connection and a fresh first frame (~0.6-1 s for a good server), and churns the provider's connection count.
problems.evidence: LivePage.kt:2524-2546; Multiview.kt:148-179 and 280-285; '20:35:02.703 Channel shown in 855 ms (... player new ...)' right after '20:35:01.818 Multiview: closed'.
problems.fix_idea: For the multiview analyst: when leaving to full screen on a tile, hand that tile's player and connection to PlayerHost instead of closing and reopening. At least keep the one live ExoPlayer object across Multiview (stop instead of release) so the 'player new' build is skipped.
problems.impact: Faster, cleaner Multiview exits, and fewer refused reconnects on 1-2 connection accounts.
problems.risk: Two classes own players today: the handover must move the lease, listeners and surface exactly once. Larger change.

problems.title: With more playlists, the guide re-reads big lists and does linear work on the main thread
problems.detail: Only one list over 2000 channels is kept. 'All playlists' is built from each playlist's All channels, and with 2 or more big playlists those push each other out. So switching between 'All playlists' and a playlist's 'All channels' re-reads 9-17k rows each time (in the background, 1-3 s on a Stick). The guide's indexChannels allocates a key and a number string per channel on the main thread, and rowOf is a linear scan (channelOf, focusChannel, refreshControls, programmeNow). Each Channel carries its full stream link (with login), so ~30k channels is roughly 12-18 MB of heap.
problems.evidence: ScopeLists.kt:39-41 and 67; LivePage.kt:1084-1091; GuideView.kt:259-269, 314, 395, 474; LiveModels.kt:59-76.
problems.fix_idea: Keep 'All playlists' as the one big list and serve each AllChannels(p) as a subList view of it: zero copy, since the order is the playlists' lists one after another. Or keep two big lists while memory allows. For lists over ~5k, build the key-to-row index as a HashMap on the guide thread and hand it over with the list. Optional later: leave the url out of guide list reads and read it by key at tune time (adds a ~ms background read before a change, so weigh it against zap speed).
problems.impact: Scales to 3+ playlists of ~9-17k channels without repeated multi-second reads or main-thread spikes when 'All playlists' is shown.
problems.risk: subList views must be invalidated with listChanges exactly as now. The list reads stay compatible both ways (no schema change).

problems.title: The remembered group per channel ('zap_group:<key>') grows with no limit in the Live TV preferences
problems.detail: Each channel ever played adds a zap_group entry. Every apply() rewrites the whole fireplayer_live file, which is also written on every guide focus move (prefs.focus). It grows faster with more playlists.
problems.evidence: LivePage.kt:2648-2653 (setZapGroupOf), 1284 (prefs.focus = channel.key in showDetails), 1794 and 1823.
problems.fix_idea: Keep only the last ~200 zap_group entries (prune the oldest when adding; a missing key already falls back via ZapOrder.candidates), and write prefs.focus only when focus settles (on leave/stop) or debounced.
problems.impact: A smaller preferences file, cheaper writes and a cheaper waitToFinish at onPause.
problems.risk: Old and new versions read the same keys; pruning is compatible both ways.

problems.title: The film glass keeps copying a surface that has no frames
problems.detail: With full-screen controls up over a dead or not-yet-started picture, the glass backdrop copies the SurfaceView twice a second. Each copy fails with a warning, so it does work for nothing.
problems.evidence: 'Surface doesn't have any previously queued frames, nothing to readback from' every ~500 ms at 21:05:42-43 and 21:06:11-12.
problems.fix_idea: Copy only after onRenderedFirstFrame for the current stream (status.playing, or a frame-rendered flag); fall back to the wallpaper glass otherwise.
problems.impact: Minor CPU and GPU savings in the failure case.
problems.risk: Low.

problems.title: Not yet verified: whether the screensaver (a DreamService on Fire OS 8) stops HomeActivity
problems.detail: While a channel plays, keepScreenOn blocks the screensaver. While paused, refused, waiting slowly or (after change 2) stuck, it can start after the Max's 60 min. If it does not stop the activity, a paused or retrying channel keeps its player or retries under the screensaver.
problems.evidence: HomeActivity.kt:1456; adb: screensaver_components=com.amazon.ftv.screensaver/.app.services.ScreensaverService, screen_off_timeout=3600000; no dream lines in tonight's log.
problems.fix_idea: TV test on the Max while no other test is running: pause a channel, start the screensaver, and check that 'ExoPlayerImpl Release' / onStop appear. If not, listen for ACTION_DREAMING_STARTED/STOPPED (a dynamic receiver while Live TV plays) and treat it like onStop/onStart.
problems.impact: Makes sure no stream or decoder lives under the screensaver.
problems.risk: Low.

findings.summary:
I went through tonight's Max log, 20:33–21:10. The main finding changes the diagnosis. The 12 minutes of "GetCmd No command in 5 seconds" (20:51:55–21:04:00) were not a decoder idling because its picture was off screen. They were a decoder whose backend had crashed. At 20:51:50.636 the MediaTek video service, vpud (pid 606), segfaulted inside its H.264 decoder (libvcodecdrv.so, H264_decode+1212). Just before that, the channel had sent a burst of damaged picture data. The restarted vpud (pid 6816) never served another decoder until the reboot.

What the viewer saw: the picture froze at 20:51:50 and the sound carried on until 20:52:17. At 20:52:17 the provider closed the stream, as it had been doing every ~27 s. The player then sat with no picture and no sound until 21:04:05, about 11 min 48 s. FirePlayer logged nothing from 20:50:36 to 21:02:58. Its stall watch only runs while buffering, and its "stream ended" recovery needs every renderer to finish, which a dead video decoder never does.

After 21:04:05:
- Releasing the player hung: the codec flush timed out (-110) and the decoder threads could not exit.
- FirePlayer then created 7 more players, 2 of them multiview pictures, on a decoder that could no longer respond. None showed a picture.
- The surface-detach timeouts that followed each froze the main thread for about 2.5 s (three "Davey" stalls of 2.56–2.68 s, 151–156 skipped frames). Key presses waited up to 5.1 s.
- The ANR came at 21:06:52 and the app was killed. After the restart, the new player spun with no message until the log ends at 21:09:16.

Before the crash, the one 720p59.94 channel (~3.2 Mb/s) was the source of most trouble:
- Its stream ended 31 times in 14 m 52 s (every 12–72 s, median 27 s). FirePlayer recovered every time in 748–1136 ms (mean 930 ms), 28.8 s of gaps in total.
- It sent damaged H.264 data all along: 801 "invalid NALU 2" lines plus 87 "un-support type of NAL" lines in 4 bursts. One burst caused a fatal decode error at 20:40:55, which FirePlayer recovered in 2.79 s. The last burst came just before the vpud crash.
- There were 0 "Live rebuffer" lines all night, and Wi-Fi was good: −55 to −62 dBm on 5 GHz, link rate 864–960 Mb/s, no disconnects. So the stream drops look like the provider, not the network.

Other events:
- At first open the provider sent something that wasn't a video stream: 11 tries over 46 s.
- The first multiview session (2 pictures) came during a memory crisis: Fire OS killed 12 other apps, freeing 518 MB, and the memory warning hit its most severe level (15). Each picture dropped about 9–10% of its frames, and the decoder driver logged 32 errors while two H.264 decoders ran at once.
- Garbage collection was never a problem (worst pause 9.4 ms).

What FirePlayer can fix itself:
- Spot a frozen picture with a cheap check every few seconds.
- After one rebuild attempt, stop making new players once the decoder is stuck, and show the plain "restart the Fire TV" message.
- Shorten the main-thread waits when a player is torn down.
- Start the 15 s first-picture check when a channel opens, not only after it has played (agreed change 2).
- Narrow the reconnect gap.
- Hand the playing player to multiview instead of rebuilding it.
- Stop downloading the same 12.9 MB guide file twice.

On the provider side: the stream drops, the damaged data and the non-video replies. On the Fire OS side: the vpud crash, the decoder service staying stuck, and the low-memory kills.

Agreed change 1 (release an idle decoder when its picture is off screen) is still good for memory, but it would not have prevented tonight. Releasing a decoder whose service has died is exactly what hangs.

problems.title: A frozen picture with no error is never noticed (12+ minutes tonight)
problems.detail: When the decoder dies under a player that is still marked ready, the player stays 'playing' with a still picture. The sound goes on until the provider next ends the stream, then stops. Media3 never reaches its ended state (the dead video decoder can't finish) and never buffers, so neither FirePlayer's stall watch nor its stream-ended recovery fires. Nothing in PlayerHost checks that frames are still coming.
problems.evidence: Video stopped at 20:51:49.629/20:51:50.636 (vpud segfault); audio end-of-stream at 20:52:17.269; no FirePlayer line 20:50:36–21:02:58. PlayerHost.kt:713-720 (reconnects only on STATE_ENDED) and :740-797 (stall checks only while buffering). The VOD player already reads renderedOutputBufferCount (PlaybackDiag.kt:150-156, 296)
problems.fix_idea: Add a 'picture moving' check every 4–5 s while the live player is ready and meant to play: read player.videoDecoderCounters rendered + dropped + skipped counts, never a per-frame callback. If they don't move for ~8–10 s while not buffering or paused, log it in one line, then rebuild the player once. If the rebuilt player shows no first frame within ~15 s, show the plain message from agreed change 2 ('The TV's video decoder isn't responding. Restarting the Fire TV should fix it.'). Skip the check when no video track is selected (radio channels), while paused, and while sound is held back by Alexa.

problems.effort: Small to medium (one Runnable on the existing main handler plus a pure rule class with unit tests, like LiveStallWatch)
problems.risk: Low with the exclusions; the threshold needs testing on very low-fps or still-image channels

problems.title: Once the decoder is stuck, FirePlayer keeps making players, which led to the ANR
problems.detail: After the codec service stopped responding, FirePlayer created 7 players, 2 of them multiview pictures. Each blocked its own playback thread for good. Leaving each one cost about 2.5 s of frozen main thread (Media3's default 2 s surface-detach wait plus 0.5 s release wait). Back-to-back teardowns pushed key latency to 5.1 s and caused the ANR. Multiview also opened on top of the stuck decoder.

Set it when the picture-moving check fails after a rebuild, when a first frame doesn't come within 15 s although the stream's tracks are known, or on a surface-detach ERROR_CODE_TIMEOUT. While it's set: create no new players or multiview pictures, show the plain message, and offer the restart hint. Leaving a stuck player would then cost under 1 s instead of 2.5 s. This lives in memory only; after a restart the 15 s first-picture rule finds the stuck decoder again.

problems.title: Stream-end reconnect gap (provider drops every ~27 s) could be shortened or mostly hidden
problems.detail: FirePlayer waits until Media3 has played out everything it had loaded (the ended state), waits a fixed 300 ms, then reconnects. That makes about 0.93 s of frozen picture and silence each time, 31 times in 15 minutes. LiveReconnect.kt:62's own comment says what was loaded has already played out by then, so the 300 ms wait buys nothing on a first try. Each reconnect also recreates the audio output (36 of them tonight) and drops about 3–10 frames on restart. The provider also restarts its stream at a different point each time (replays up to 6.7 s or skips up to 10.4 s).
problems.evidence: 31 'stream ended; try 1 in 300 ms' → 'playing again after 748–1136 ms'; 'the latest buffer is 1025–1255 old'; 36 AUDIOINFO lines; 20 PTS jumps −6.74..+10.41 s
problems.fix_idea: (a) Use 0–50 ms instead of 300 ms for the first reconnect after a stream end: about 0.3 s saved each time, ~9 s tonight. (b) Measure before building more: one log line per stream end saying how much was still loaded when the connection closed (Media3 reports the load completing). If ~1–3 s typically remains, start the new connection at that moment, so the old buffer covers the 0.5–0.8 s it takes to open the new one. (c) Later, since the user plans more playlists: after for example 5 drops in 3 minutes, offer to play the same channel from another playlist, the way films move to the next source.
problems.impact: Medium. This is the 'channel lagging' the user notices most often on bad provider nights.
problems.risk: (a) A provider that refuses instant reconnects would show up as failed tries, which the existing backoff already handles

problems.title: The same 12.9 MB guide file is downloaded again for a second playlist from the same provider
problems.detail: The user added a playlist from the same provider (same default name). Its guide was the same 12,936 KB size and took another 4.6 s to download, parse and store.

problems.title: The glass backdrop keeps trying to copy a video surface that has no picture
problems.detail: While the decoder had no frame, the glass backdrop's copy of the video surface failed every 500 ms. Harmless, but it is wasted work, and the comment says probes can run up to ten times a second.

problems.title: System CPU at ~45% during plain 720p60 live playback; not yet attributed
problems.detail: System CPU was 45–46% while one hardware-decoded 720p60 channel played full screen, against 6% while frozen. The log can't say how much is FirePlayer: candidates include the playback loop, TS parsing, software AAC decoding, Dolby audio processing in the audio service, composition, and the glass backdrop's copies.
problems.evidence: perfmonitord 'CPUUtilization is at 45%' (20:36:22), '46%' (20:46:23), '6%' (20:56:24); in the ANR block 'fireos.hardware.audio.service' 10%, surfaceflinger 12%
problems.fix_idea: Measure per thread (top -H -p <pid> for a minute) during live full screen and with 3 multiview pictures on the Max before changing anything. Act only on FirePlayer threads that show up.
problems.impact: Unknown (it could matter for keeping multiview lean)
problems.risk: None

problems.title: Out of FirePlayer's hands: provider stream drops, damaged data, and the vendor decoder crash
problems.detail: The 720p channel dropped its connection every 12–72 s while Wi-Fi was clean. It sent damaged H.264 data continuously, and twice that broke the decoder: a recoverable fatal error, then the vpud segfault. Fire OS didn't recover the codec service after vpud restarted; only a reboot did. The first channel attempts got replies that weren't a stream, and <playlist B>'s guide wasn't valid XML. The periodic drops may come from the provider's connection limit if the other TV was playing the same line at the time, which is worth checking against the playlist's max-connections value. Fire OS also killed 12 other apps (518 MB) while the first picture and multiview started.
problems.evidence: Wi-Fi metrics (rssi −55..−62, phyrate 864–960); 801 + 87 VPUD bitstream errors; 'Fatal signal 11 ... (vpud)' with 'H264_decode+1212'; no decoder served by vpud 6816; 'XmlPullParserException'; 12 lmk kills 20:34:24–20:34:55
problems.fix_idea: FirePlayer's part is to detect these and say so plainly (items above). Optionally offer the same channel from another playlist when one keeps dropping. Software decoding of the bundled FFmpeg video for 720p after a decoder crash could be tested on the Max, but there is no evidence yet that the Max can sustain 720p60 that way. Report the vpud crash (tombstone_12) upstream if a channel is known to trigger it.
problems.impact: Context for what can't be fixed in the app
problems.risk: n/a

findings.summary:
On-device measurement on the Max (<ip> only; I never touched 6556). FirePlayer 1.0.374, pid 4937. I changed no settings, playlists or favourites, and made no code edits.

As found, the user's multiview had 3 pictures with NBA 01 large on top. The bottom-left picture (EPIX2) had been frozen for about 57 minutes. During that time it had no network socket, its OMX decoder sat idle and logged "GetCmd() line: 453 No command in 5 seconds" every 5 s, and FirePlayer wrote no log line about it, so nothing tried to recover it.

The other bottom picture (Cinemax Hits East) kept seeing its provider stream "end" every 17-56 s (26 times in 14 minutes). Each time it reconnected by itself, but every reconnect left that picture without a picture for about 3.8 s and jumped the content by -4 to +11 s.

Measured costs:
- **Memory as found:** app PSS was 510 MB, 364 MB of it graphics. MemAvailable was 158 MB, swap was 92% used and CMA free was 0.
- **Memory with a freshly opened 3-picture view:** PSS 253 MB, graphics 117 MB.
- **Memory with one channel full screen:** PSS 163 MB, graphics 17 MB, MemAvailable 624 MB.
- **Graphics growth from layout changes:** each multiview layout change (OK on a picture) adds about 14 MB of graphics memory. In my test it went from 178 MB to 275 MB after 10 changes. This is HWUI GPU cache (148 MB, of which 144 MB can be freed) and multiview never trims it.
- **CPU (out of 400%):** app 47-65%, surfaceflinger 30% (10% full screen), vpud 15-19%, three AAC software decoders 13-18%, audio HAL 15%.
- **Composition:** two of the three video layers (the 1080p sources) are composited by the GPU (CLIENT). SurfaceFlinger missed about 15 frames/s against 0.05/s full screen, and hwcomposer logged 147 slow-blit waits per minute against 15-40 full screen.
- **Per-picture video size:** small pictures still decode 1080p, because the maxVideo cap per picture role does nothing on single-rendition TS streams.

Geometry at 1920x1080 px (dp = px/2):
- **Equal grid:** cells of 917x516 px with 16 px gaps and 35 px side margins. The "Add a channel" cell is a full-size cell at 968,548-1885,1064 (bottom right). The grid is already limited by height and uses 96% of the width.
- **Large-on-top (3 pictures):** large picture 352,16-1568,700 (1216x684), small ones 333,716-952,1064 and 968,716-1587,1064. That covers 61% of the screen, with 333-352 px of black at each side.
- **Two side by side:** about 936x527 px each, covering 47.5% of the screen.
- **Corners and switching:** corner radius is 12 dp (24 px) on every picture size. Layouts switch with OK on a picture (large on top ↔ equal grid).

Open and close timings:
- **Opening 2 pictures:** first frames 3.15 s and 3.65 s after the pick; UI 5% janky.
- **Adding a third picture:** 4.2 s.
- **Closing:** the three players are released one after another on the main thread in 230-450 ms. Remote key latency was 673 ms once. The full-screen channel then shows in 2.8-3.1 s.

Zapping: 8 channel up/down presses took 1.4-4.4 s from key to first frame, mostly about 4.2 s. FirePlayer's own share is about 100 ms (open 7-10 ms, decoder 27-60 ms). The rest is the provider: a redirect connection at +1.0 s, first bytes at +5.2 s.

Off-screen decoder:
- **Movies page:** the player is released within 1 s.
- **Fire TV Home key:** the player is released about 1.9 s after the key, with 0 decoders and 0% CPU.
- **FirePlayer Home:** the live tile keeps playing, and it keeps the decoder, the stream, the audio and 23-30% CPU even with the rows scrolled so the tile is off screen (watched for 70 s+). That is the case agreed change (1) should cover.

Single-channel rebuffers in the guide miniature lasted 7.5-21 s. The after-stall cushion grows 3 → 6 → 9 s and the stall watch never fired.

I left the Max as found: multiview open with 3 pictures, NBA 01 (<playlist>) large on top, selected and heard; EPIX2 (<playlist>) bottom left, now playing; Cinemax Hits East (<playlist>) bottom right. Temporary screenshots on the device were removed, nothing else was left on it, and the log stream has stopped.

facts.claim: The as-found bottom-left multiview picture (EPIX2) was frozen for about 57 minutes with no recovery and no FirePlayer log line.
facts.evidence: SurfaceFlinger --latency for layer 'SurfaceView ... HomeActivity#2' (geomLayerTransform 333,716 = bottom-left): 127 frames between uptime 460.3 and 586.7 s with a 123 s gap, and nothing after that; the sample was taken at uptime about 3425 s, and boot was about 21:14:20, so the picture was frozen from about 21:24 until I closed multiview at 22:21. App sockets were 'st01 rx0 rp80' x2, i.e. only 2 sockets for 3 pictures. OMX thread 9606 logged '11-27 22:01:47.459 607 9606 W MtkOmxVdecExV4L2: ## [WARNING, 110] GetCmd() line: 453 No command in 5 seconds ...' every 5 s until the release at 22:21:15. Loader thread 9597 used 0 CPU ticks in 10 s. No FirePlayerLive line mentioned the picture.

facts.claim: The other bottom picture's provider stream 'ended' every 17-56 s and FirePlayer reconnected it by itself each time, but each reconnect cost about 3.8 s with no picture plus a content jump.
facts.evidence: 26 'Multiview recovery: a picture's stream ended; try 1 in 300 ms' lines in 14 min as found (intervals 17.1-56.4 s); 41 over the session. Codec EOS to 'Rendering first frame' took 2.97-7.11 s (mean 3.81 s). PTS jumps at reconnect were -4.3 to +11.4 s ('Possible seek found! last pts:1002843174000 cur pts:1002840371000'). One 15 s outage hit 2 pictures at once (22:37:28 to 22:37:43).
