problems.title: A multiview picture can freeze silently and stay frozen for good
problems.detail: One picture showed a still frame for about 57 min. It had no connection and an idle decoder, and no watcher acted. MultiviewPlayer only reacts to an error, to STATE_ENDED, or to READY→BUFFERING while not 'jumping' (noteStall). A picture that sits in any other state without new frames is never noticed. This is the same gap as agreed change (2), seen in multiview.
problems.evidence: measure_m1_multiview_as_found.txt: idle-decoder lines from thread 9606 every 5 s; SurfaceFlinger latency for layer #2 shows no frame after uptime 586.7 s; only 2 sockets for 3 pictures; no FirePlayerLive line. MultiviewPlayer.kt noteStall() and stallCheck.
problems.fix_idea: One cheap watch per picture (and for the full-screen player), checked every 4 s and never per frame. If the picture should be playing but its rendered-frame count (DecoderCounters.renderedOutputBufferCount, or the time of the last onRenderedFirstFrame/onVideoFrameProcessingOffset) has not moved for about 12-15 s, release that player and reopen it. If a fresh open also shows nothing within 15 s, show the plain message about the TV's video decoder. Reuse LiveStallWatch-style pure logic so it can be unit-tested.
problems.impact: high: removes 'frozen picture forever', which the user has to fix by hand today
problems.risk: low, provided reopening releases the old player before making a new one

problems.title: HWUI GPU cache grows with every multiview layout change and is never trimmed
problems.detail: Each OK (large ↔ grid) adds about 14 MB of graphics memory at first, about 100 MB after 10 changes, and up to 364 MB in the as-found session. 144 MB of it can be freed, but nothing frees it while multiview stays open, and MemAvailable was down to 158-204 MB.
problems.evidence: measure_m3_open_close.txt: GL mtrack 177,727 → 263,621 → 275,003 KB; gfxinfo 'Scratch Texture 117.02 MB (475 entries)', 'Total GPU memory usage 148.29 MB (144.21 MB is purgeable)'; as found GL 364,001 KB; GraphicsTrim.kt is used by PlayerActivity and FilmMode but not by Multiview.
problems.fix_idea: When a board move settles (moveEnd) and when the picker closes, schedule a single GraphicsTrim.trim(minGap), or on this Fire OS, where staleOnly is true, a trim STALE_MS + 1 s later. That is one Runnable, nothing per frame. Also check whether the per-frame scale transform of Picture views, with the anti-aliased corner path drawn under scale, is what creates the 475 scratch textures. If it is, hide the corner path during the move or draw corners only at rest.
problems.impact: high for memory (100-250 MB) on a 1.7 GB TV
problems.risk: low

problems.title: Small multiview pictures still decode and composite full 1080p
problems.detail: setMaxVideoSize has no effect on single-rendition TS channels. Each small picture holds a 1080p decoder with its 1080p buffers, and its layer is downscaled by the GPU (CLIENT composition). Result: surfaceflinger at 30% CPU, about 15 missed frames/s, many slow blits, and 51-67% UI jank during reconnect spinners.
problems.evidence: HWC table: 2 CLIENT layers with 1920x1080 crop, 1 DEVICE with 1280x720; 'updateFormatChanged width = 1920 height = 1080' for EQUAL/SMALL pictures; missed frames +303 in 20 s against +1 in 20 s full screen.
problems.fix_idea: The resolution can't be lowered by track selection, so: (a) keep the number of pictures that are both CLIENT-composited and large small, e.g. the user's new 3-picture layout should keep tile sizes the HWC accepts (worth measuring which sizes and source scales stay DEVICE); (b) test SurfaceView.setZOrderMediaOverlay / no-corner-overlay variants to see whether the black corner overlay forces client composition; (c) cap multiview at what the decoders and HWC can carry well. Needs a short on-device experiment before deciding.
problems.impact: medium-high (smoothness, CPU, heat)
problems.risk: medium

problems.title: Unheard pictures still decode audio
problems.detail: All pictures decode AAC in software and feed AudioFlinger at -inf dB, so 2 of the 3 decoders do wasted work.
problems.evidence: media.swcodec 'oid.aac.decoder' at 4.7% + 4.2% + 0.5%; media.swcodec 12.6-17.8% in multiview against 7% full screen; audio_flinger shows a second active app track at -inf dB; MultiviewPlayer.kt doc says 'the sound always decoded'.
problems.fix_idea: Disable the audio track type (setTrackTypeDisabled(C.TRACK_TYPE_AUDIO, true)) on pictures that aren't heard, and enable it on the selected one. That costs a short audio start (a few hundred ms) when the selection moves. Alternatively disable it only for pictures unselected for more than N seconds.
problems.impact: medium (about 8-10% CPU, plus audio HAL and mixer load)
problems.risk: low-medium (audio start delay when moving the selection)

problems.title: Live tile on FirePlayer Home keeps decoder, stream and audio while scrolled off screen
problems.detail: This is the remaining case for agreed change (1). The Movies page and the Fire TV Home key already let the player go within about 1-2 s.
problems.evidence: measure_m5_offscreen.txt: Home scrolled 3 rows down → omx_decoders=1, app CPU 23-30% for 70 s, audio track active at 0 dB; Movies → Release within 1 s; Fire TV Home → Release 1.9 s after the key.
problems.fix_idea: When the live tile's view is not visible on screen (or its page is hidden) for about 30-60 s, release the player and keep the channel. When the tile comes back into view, reopen it (about 2.8-3 s with this provider), showing the last frame or the logo meanwhile. Check visibility on scroll and visibility events, not per frame.
problems.impact: medium (frees about 25% CPU, one decoder, bandwidth, and the idle-decoder risk)
problems.risk: low

problems.title: Each multiview reconnect costs about 3.8 s with no picture; the provider ends streams every 17-56 s
problems.detail: Recovery works by itself, but often: 26 times in 14 min on one picture, sometimes 2 pictures at once (15 s). Most of the time goes to waiting for the provider's first byte, about 4 s.
problems.evidence: EOS→first frame 2.97-7.11 s (mean 3.81 s); 'stream ended; try 1 in 300 ms' every 17-56 s; zap socket trace: first bytes at +5.2 s after the key.
problems.fix_idea: Keep the last frame on screen (no black) and delay the spinner until about 1.5 s into a reconnect (BusySigns probably already delays it; check). Consider reopening the stream at about 80% of the observed 'ends every N s' period, before it ends, so the gap disappears. Only worth it if the provider allows the overlap, and this playlist allows only limited streams, so it probably isn't usable here. At the very least, count ends per picture in the log so the diagnosis is quick.
problems.impact: medium (what the user sees as 'channel lagging')
problems.risk: pre-reconnect needs a second connection; not possible within the account's stream allowance

problems.title: Closing multiview blocks the main thread while releasing players one after another
problems.detail: ExoPlayer.release() runs three times on the main thread. That took 230-450 ms, with a 673 ms key-latency report. In tonight's incident, one release hung on a failed codec flush.
problems.evidence: 'ExoPlayerImpl: Release' on thread 4937/4937 at 22:21:14.917, 15.083 and 15.151; 'Multiview: closed' at 15.236; 'key event latency ... Latency: 673'.
problems.fix_idea: Stop and detach the surfaces first (cheap), then release the players with a short timeout (setReleaseTimeoutMs, already available in Media3), or post each release so the UI and the next channel's open aren't held up. Keep releasing before opening the full-screen player so decoders are freed.
problems.impact: medium (snappier close, protects against the incident's hang)
problems.risk: low

problems.title: Single-channel rebuffers drag on for 12-21 s because the after-stall cushion keeps growing
problems.detail: The cushion grows 3 → 6 → 9 s, and the stall watch never fires while data trickles in. Reopening the stream costs about 4 s with this provider.
problems.evidence: 'Live rebuffer 3: ... plays on at 9000 ms loaded' then 'Live rebuffer over after 12421 ms'; 'Live rebuffer over after 20982 ms'; LiveStallWatch LIMIT_MS 12000, PROGRESS_MS 500.
problems.fix_idea: Cap the wait: if a rebuffer goes on for more than about 8 s and refill is slower than real time, reconnect at the live edge instead of waiting for a 9 s cushion. Or cap the after-stall need at about 6 s. Pure rule, unit-testable.
problems.impact: medium
problems.risk: low-medium (more reconnects on genuinely slow feeds)

problems.title: Layout uses little of the screen with 2 pictures and with large-on-top
problems.detail: Side by side covers 47.5% of the screen and large-on-top covers 61%. The equal grid is already limited by height (cells 917x516; only shrinking the 8 dp gaps and margins gains about 2%). The Add cell takes a full picture-size cell. This bears on the user's 3-picture request: bottom picture centred, smaller Add to its right.
problems.evidence: View bounds in measure_m2_top.txt and measure_m2_grid_bounds.txt; MultiviewRules.kt grid/sideBySide/withLarge; full-size screencaps.
problems.fix_idea: 3-picture equal layout: 2 on top at full cell size, the third centred under them at the same size (x = (1920-917)/2 = 501 px), Add as a smaller square or 16:9 button (about 1/3 of a cell) to its right in the leftover strip (from 1418 px to 1885 px, 467 px wide). Consider a smaller corner radius (for example 8 dp, 16 px) for 'less cropped'. With 2 pictures, nothing larger is possible at 16:9 side by side; only tighter margins help.
problems.impact: user-requested
problems.risk: low (pure layout maths, unit-tested)

findings.summary:
Research on Media3 1.8.0 for Fire TV MediaTek devices. I checked it three ways: bytecode of the 1.8.0 jars in the gradle cache (javap dumps in <scratchpad>/m3/ as eii.txt, epi.txt, mcvr.txt, mcr.txt, rh.txt), read-only probes of the Max (codec XML, media.resource_manager, SurfaceFlinger, features; no key presses), and public docs and issues. Each fact is marked [VERIFIED] (bytecode, device, doc or log quote) or [INFERRED].

Main conclusions:
1. A wedged MTK decoder blocks ExoPlayer's playback thread inside a native MediaCodec call. Nothing in Media3 1.8.0 detects that.
   - Every main-thread call that waits on that thread then costs its timeout: about 2000 ms to replace or clear a surface, then 500 ms for release().
   - 2000 + 500 ms fits the 2574 ms "Davey" stall and the 151/152 skipped frames tonight. Two or three players touched like that cross the 5 s ANR limit.
2. In 1.8.0 every stop() or release() flushes the video codec before releasing it. On the Max that runs through SynchronousMediaCodecAdapter, because Media3 only uses the async adapter on API 31+ or on Fire TVs that have the tv_screen feature, and the Max has neither. That flush is exactly the call that timed out at 21:04:08.
3. clearVideoSurfaceView or setVideoSurface(null) does NOT free the decoder on the Max. It moves the codec onto a hidden placeholder surface and keeps decoding. stop() or disabling the video track does free it.
4. Using the same player when switching channels (or reconnecting from ENDED) keeps the decoder. Tonight's log shows 31 reconnects with only 2 decoder creations. stop() throws the decoder away.
5. The Max's own codec file says AVC and HEVC allow 5 instances each, secure decoders 1. Throughput is about 2.2M blocks/s, roughly 271 frames per second at 1080p.
6. Max video size and bitrate limits only choose between variants. They do not reduce decoding work for single-rendition MPEG-TS.
7. Dynamic scheduling in 1.8.0 does nothing while video plays. Video support came in 1.10.0 and it became the default in 1.11.0.

Sources I could not open from this session: developer.amazon.com, lightrun.com and ffmpeg.org do not resolve here; they need adding to the session's network settings. GitHub issue pages opened fine. Amazon guidance is cited only from search-result summaries.

During my probes another session was using FirePlayer on the Max (pid 4937; its decoder count changed while I looked). My probes were read-only.

facts.claim: [VERIFIED] Default timeouts in 1.8.0: release() and setForegroundMode() wait up to 500 ms; detaching or replacing a surface waits up to 2000 ms. Both report a timeout through onPlayerError.
facts.evidence: javap -constants on media3-exoplayer-1.8.0: ExoPlayer.DEFAULT_RELEASE_TIMEOUT_MS = 500l, DEFAULT_DETACH_SURFACE_TIMEOUT_MS = 2000l. Docs (developer.android.com/reference/androidx/media3/exoplayer/ExoPlayer.Builder): setReleaseTimeoutMs 'If a call to release or setForegroundMode takes more than timeoutMs to complete, the player will report an error via onPlayerError'; setDetachSurfaceTimeoutMs 'If detaching a surface or replacing a surface takes more than detachSurfaceTimeoutMs to complete, the player will report an error via onPlayerError'.

facts.claim: [VERIFIED] What release() does on timeout: the app thread blocks for up to releaseTimeoutMs. If time runs out, listeners still registered get ERROR_CODE_TIMEOUT (1003), then ExoPlayerImpl cleans up its own side. The playback thread is NOT interrupted; it stays in its blocked call and runs MSG_RELEASE only if it ever returns. release() returns at once if the playback thread is already dead.
facts.evidence: ExoPlayerImplInternal.release(): posts message 7, then ConditionVariable.blockUninterruptible(releaseTimeoutMs), returning true early when !playbackLooper.getThread().isAlive(). ExoPlayerImpl.release() offsets 127-147: if internalPlayer.release() is false it sends lambda$release$6 = onPlayerError(createForUnexpected(new ExoTimeoutException(1 = TIMEOUT_OPERATION_RELEASE), 1003)). It then calls listeners.release(), removeSurfaceCallbacks(), ownedSurface.release() and sets playerReleased.

facts.claim: [VERIFIED] When the surface wait happens: only when an existing surface is replaced by a different one, including null. Attaching a surface to a player that has none never waits. On timeout the player is stopped with ExoTimeoutException(TIMEOUT_OPERATION_DETACH_SURFACE) and ERROR_CODE_TIMEOUT. clearVideoSurfaceView, and SurfaceHolder.Callback.surfaceDestroyed (a SurfaceView hidden or removed while still attached), both take this same blocking path on the main thread.
facts.evidence: ExoPlayerImpl.setVideoOutputInternal bytecode: waits detachSurfaceTimeoutMs only if videoOutput != null && videoOutput != new, otherwise C.TIME_UNSET; if internalPlayer.setVideoOutput(...) is false then stopInternal(createForUnexpected(new ExoTimeoutException(3), 1003)). clearVideoSurfaceView -> clearVideoSurfaceHolder -> clearVideoSurface(). ComponentListener.surfaceDestroyed -> setVideoOutputInternal.

facts.claim: [VERIFIED] Why the playback thread died tonight: one codec error during release leaves the other renderers half-released, then the thread quits. Release runs in try/finally. Disabling renderers stops at the first one that throws ('Disable failed.' / 'Reset failed.' are only logged). The next renderer still enabled then fails BaseRenderer.release's state check ('Unexpected runtime error'). The finally block still quits the looper, so later posts hit a dead thread.
facts.evidence: ExoPlayerImplInternal.releaseInternal: resetInternal; releaseRenderers; ... finally PlaybackLooperProvider.releaseLooper() and ConditionVariable.open(). disableRenderers() loops disableRenderer(i) with no catch per renderer. BaseRenderer.release() = checkState(state == 0). Log: 21:04:08.381 'E/ExoPlayerImplInternal: Disable failed.' (MediaCodec.native_flush, SynchronousMediaCodecAdapter.flush, MediaCodecRenderer.onDisabled); 21:04:08.403 'Reset failed.' (MediaCodec.native_stop); 21:04:08.413 'Unexpected runtime error ... BaseRenderer.release(BaseRenderer.java:260)'; 21:04:08.443 'sending message to a Handler on a dead thread' from DefaultAudioSink.releaseAudioTrackAsync.

facts.claim: [VERIFIED] In 1.8.0, stopping or releasing a player always FLUSHES the video codec first, then releases it (stop + release). Media3 skips the flush only for its built-in workarounds, and the switches for that are final in MediaCodecVideoRenderer.
facts.evidence: MediaCodecRenderer.onDisabled -> flushOrReleaseCodec -> flushCodec unless shouldReleaseCodecInsteadOfFlushing(); onReset -> releaseCodec. MediaCodecVideoRenderer: 'protected final boolean shouldReleaseCodecInsteadOfFlushing()' and 'protected final boolean shouldFlushCodec()'. Same order in tonight's stack traces (evidence lines 3538-3545 and 3559-3564).

facts.claim: [VERIFIED] The flush can be skipped from app code, but only where a release follows anyway. A renderer subclass can call releaseCodec() before super.onDisabled(), because the flush step returns at once when there is no codec. [INFERRED] That removes one OMX port-flush round trip. The release itself still moves the component Executing->Idle, which also hung tonight. Doing it on every disable would also break decoder reuse when switching channels on the same player (see the channel-switch fact).
facts.evidence: MediaCodecRenderer: 'protected void releaseCodec()'; private flushOrReleaseCodec begins 'if (codec == null) return false'. MediaCodecVideoRenderer.onDisabled is protected and not final. The app already wraps renderers (player/PlayerFactory.kt:1308 and :1322 extend ForwardingRenderer; LiveRenderersFactory). Log 21:04:12.397 'failed to enter Idle state (now Executing(3), aborting'.

facts.claim: [VERIFIED] The Max uses the synchronous codec adapter. Media3's default picks the asynchronous one only on API 31+, or on API 28+ when the system feature com.amazon.hardware.tv_screen exists. The Max is API 30 and has no tv_screen feature.
facts.evidence: DefaultMediaCodecAdapterFactory.shouldUseAsynchronousAdapterInDefaultMode: SDK_INT >= 31, or (context != null && SDK_INT >= 28 && hasSystemFeature("com.amazon.hardware.tv_screen")). Max: getprop ro.build.version.sdk = 30; 'pm list features | grep -c tv_screen' = 0. Log stack 'SynchronousMediaCodecAdapter.flush(SynchronousMediaCodecAdapter.java:160)'. [INFERRED] forceEnableMediaCodecAsynchronousQueueing() would not help with hangs: flush and release still run synchronously on the playback thread, and it adds threads per codec.

facts.claim: [VERIFIED] Clearing the surface does NOT free the decoder on the Max. The renderer swaps the codec onto a PlaceholderSurface and it keeps decoding the hidden picture at full cost. The Amazon models in Media3's 'no output-surface swap' workaround list do not include AFTKRT.
facts.evidence: MediaCodecVideoRenderer.setOutput: when SDK_INT >= 23, the codec is not null, hasSurfaceForCodec() and !codecNeedsSetOutputSurfaceWorkaround, it calls setOutputSurface(codec, getSurfaceForCodec()); otherwise releaseCodec(). shouldUsePlaceholderSurface = SDK>=23 && !tunneling && !codecNeedsSetOutputSurfaceWorkaround(name) && (!secure || PlaceholderSurface.isSecureSupported). Detached surface needs API 35. Workaround strings include AFTA, AFTN, AFTR, AFTEU011, AFTEU014, AFTEUFF014, AFTJMST12, AFTKMST12, AFTSO001 (checked against Build.MODEL), not AFTKRT. Log 21:04:05.302 '[OMX.MTK.VIDEO.DECODER.AVC] setting surface generation to 3793929', 12 ms before 'Release 46c6b39'.

facts.claim: [VERIFIED] stop() does free the decoders in Media3's default mode (foreground mode off). The player object, its playback thread and its listeners stay, and prepare() resumes. Disabling the video track also frees the video decoder while the sound keeps playing. The app's comments saying a stopped player still holds its decoders are not accurate for 1.8.0.
facts.evidence: stopInternal(force, ack) -> resetInternal(force || !foregroundMode, false, true, false) -> RendererHolder.reset -> onReset -> releaseCodec; then loadControl.onStopped. Track disable: reselectTracksInternal -> enableRenderers, which calls RendererHolder.reset() for every renderer the new selection does not enable. App comments: playback/PlayerHost.kt:546 and playback/MultiviewPlayer.kt:183 ('a stopped player still holds its decoders').

facts.claim: [VERIFIED] Switching channels on the same player keeps the decoder when it can be reused. prepare and source replacement disable the renderers (with a flush) but do not reset them, so the next format is checked for reuse. Reuse is refused for: a MIME change (8), rotation (1024), a resolution change on a non-adaptive codec (512), colour info (2048), a device workaround, a size above the codec's maximum (256), or an input size above the maximum (64). The MTK AVC and HEVC decoders are adaptive.
facts.evidence: resetInternal flags per caller: prepareInternal (false,false,false,true); handleMediaSourceListInfoRefreshed (false,false,false,true); stopInternal (resetRenderers = force||!foregroundMode); releaseInternal (true,...). MediaCodecInfo.canReuseCodec bytecode checks sampleMimeType (8), rotationDegrees (1024), width/height with 'adaptive' (512), colorInfo (2048), needsAdaptationReconfigureWorkaround. MediaCodecVideoRenderer.canReuseCodec adds 256 and 64. MediaCodecVideoRenderer.getCodecMaxValues is protected. The result reaches AnalyticsListener.onVideoInputFormatChanged(eventTime, format, DecoderReuseEvaluation). Device XML: AVC/HEVC 'adaptive-playback'.

facts.claim: [VERIFIED from tonight's log] Reconnecting from ENDED with seekToDefaultPosition() + prepare() reused the decoder. A healthy decoder starts in 33-138 ms on the Max.
facts.evidence: live_evidence.txt 20:35-20:51: 96 'Live recovery' lines, about 31 'stream ended' reconnects, but only 2 'makeComponentInstance' lines (grep -c). Timing lines: 20:34:24.682 'Channel shown in 4230 ms (... player reused; tracks at 3133 ms; video decoder 138 ms)' and 20:35:02.703 '... player new; ... video decoder 33 ms'.

facts.claim: [VERIFIED in part] On a live TS (progressive) stream, a seek is a reconnect that keeps the decoder. The period forces position 0 when the stream can't seek, cancels the loader (the next load opens a new connection) and resets its sample queues. Only stop() throws the decoder away. [INFERRED] The stream-type check that skips the in-buffer seek for live progressive streams is read from the bytecode shape (it reads dataType), not from a quoted source line.
facts.evidence: ProgressiveMediaPeriod.seekToUs bytecode: seekMap.isSeekable(); reads dataType and loadingFinished; seekInsideBufferUs; Loader.cancelLoading(); SampleQueue.reset(). App retry: playback/PlayerHost.kt about line 609 'if (p.playbackState == Player.STATE_BUFFERING) p.stop()' before seekToDefaultPosition()/prepare().

facts.claim: [VERIFIED] Dynamic scheduling in 1.8.0 does not reduce work while video plays. Only the audio renderer reports a longer wait, and every started renderer otherwise asks for 10 ms. Video support arrived in 1.10.0 and the feature became default-on in 1.11.0. Stuck-player detection (StuckPlayerException) arrived in 1.9.0.
facts.evidence: javap: getDurationToProgressUs is overridden in MediaCodecAudioRenderer and MediaCodecRenderer but not in MediaCodecVideoRenderer. Renderer default: STARTED -> 10000 us; enabled and ready or ended -> 1000000 us. RELEASENOTES.md (raw.githubusercontent.com/androidx/media/release): 1.10.0 'Add support for dynamic scheduling in MediaCodecVideoRenderer to better align scheduling work and CPU wake-cycles'; 1.11.0 'Enable dynamic scheduling by default.'; 1.9.0 'Add a stuck player detection that triggers a StuckPlayerException player error if the player seems stuck'. The 1.8.0 jar has no stuck-detection setters.

facts.claim: [INFERRED] Media3's own stuck-player detection (1.9+) would not catch tonight's failure. It runs inside the playback thread's work loop, which cannot run while that thread is blocked in MediaCodec. Its default buffering limit is also 10 minutes.
facts.evidence: Docs: DEFAULT_STUCK_BUFFERING_DETECTION_TIMEOUT_MS = 600000. The playback thread was blocked in native codec calls (stack traces above; 'OMXClient: IOmx service obtained' at 21:05:55.464 and 21:06:05.836 with no makeComponentInstance after them).

facts.claim: [VERIFIED] A decoder that hangs while being created raises no error. DecoderInitializationException (ERROR_CODE_DECODER_INIT_FAILED 4001) appears only when creating or configuring the codec fails, and decoder fallback only covers that case. These APIs exist in 1.8.0 for building a watchdog: ExoPlayer.getPlaybackLooper(), isReleased(), and AnalyticsListener.onVideoDecoderInitialized, onRenderedFirstFrame and onVideoCodecError. The app already has a playback-thread heartbeat, ThreadBeat, used by the film player.
facts.evidence: javap ExoPlayer: getPlaybackLooper(), isReleased(), getVideoDecoderCounters(); AnalyticsListener: onVideoDecoderInitialized(EventTime,String,long,long), onRenderedFirstFrame(EventTime,Object,long), onVideoCodecError(EventTime,Exception). facts.claim: [VERIFIED] Keeping the last frame while switching or reconnecting. The maintainer called it device-specific, said the shutter is removed only after the first new frame is released, and suggested overriding canReuseCodec to force a fresh codec where needed. PlayerView's keep-content setting only affects PlayerView's shutter; FirePlayer uses plain SurfaceViews, so a frame stays until a new one arrives or the surface is destroyed.

Maintainers advise against releasing on a background thread, because hardware codecs would then be held for an uncontrolled time.

problems.title: A wedged decoder freezes the app's main thread and causes the ANR
problems.detail: Today each live or multiview player is closed with clearVideoSurfaceView() and then release(). When the playback thread is stuck in MediaCodec, the first call waits up to 2000 ms and the second up to 500 ms, all on the main thread. Closing or replacing 2-3 players (multiview opening after a failure) passes the 5 s input limit. A player whose thread is stuck can never clear its surface anyway.
problems.evidence: ExoPlayerImpl.setVideoOutputInternal and ExoPlayerImplInternal.release bytecode (waits of 2000 and 500 ms); playback/PlayerHost.kt:547-549 and the releasePlayer() steps in playback/MultiviewPlayer.kt (clearVideoSurfaceView, then release); log 21:05:49-50 'ERROR_CODE_TIMEOUT', 'Skipped 151 frames', 'Davey! duration=2574ms'; ANR at 21:06:37.
problems.fix_idea: Check the existing ThreadBeat (player/ThreadBeat.kt) before closing a player. If its thread has been silent for more than about 1 s, skip clearVideoSurfaceView and call release() only (at most 500 ms; could be lowered with setReleaseTimeoutMs on live and multiview players). Give the next player a fresh SurfaceView, because the stuck codec may still own the old surface. Option: setDetachSurfaceTimeoutMs of about 750-1000 ms on live players, so even an unexpected wait costs less [INFERRED].
problems.impact: Removes the 2.5 s main-thread freezes and the ANR cascade after a decoder failure.
problems.risk: Too low a surface timeout on a healthy but slow device would raise false ERROR_CODE_TIMEOUT errors. Reusing the same SurfaceView while an old codec still holds it fails to connect, which is why a fresh view is needed.

problems.title: Idle or hidden pictures keep a hardware decoder busy (agreed change 1)
problems.detail: On the Max, clearing the surface does not free the decoder: the codec moves to a hidden placeholder surface and keeps decoding. A paused channel keeps its decoder until the paused-channel timer (PausedRoom.LIVE_MS) releases the player. Tonight a decoder sat with no commands for 12 minutes, and releasing it then is what wedged the driver.
problems.evidence: MediaCodecVideoRenderer.setOutput / shouldUsePlaceholderSurface bytecode; AFTKRT is not in Media3's surface-workaround list; log 21:04:05.302 'setting surface generation' then 'Release'; playback/PlayerHost.kt:322-347 (parkPaused).
problems.fix_idea: After N seconds off screen with no sound needed, call player.stop(). That frees the decoder, the connection and the buffer, and keeps the player, so coming back is prepare() + seekToDefaultPosition(). If the sound should go on, disable only the video track (setTrackTypeDisabled(C.TRACK_TYPE_VIDEO, true)), which also frees the video decoder. Correct the comments that say a stopped player keeps its decoders.
problems.impact: Fewer decoders held, less device memory (about 37 MB of video buffers per 1080p picture), and no more releasing a decoder that has sat idle for a long time.
problems.risk: Coming back costs one decoder start (33-138 ms on the Max) and a reconnect. Turning the video track back on for a live TS stream may force a reconnect; needs a TV test.

problems.title: A first open that never shows a picture spins forever (agreed change 2)
problems.detail: The stall watch starts only after the first play. Media3 raises nothing when creating a decoder hangs; it only reports a failed creation. Its 1.9+ stuck detection runs on the blocked thread itself, so it would not fire either.
problems.evidence: PlayerHost.kt:753-755 (stallWatch starts when a stall begins); log 21:05:55.464 and 21:06:05.836 'IOmx service obtained' with no makeComponentInstance after them; androidx/media#3421.
problems.fix_idea: On open, post one delayed check (about 15 s) and cancel it on onRenderedFirstFrame. When it fires: if ThreadBeat has been silent, or the format is known but onVideoDecoderInitialized never came (healthy is under 150 ms), show the plain message that the TV's video decoder isn't responding and a restart of the Fire TV may be needed. Otherwise show the network or provider reason. Also mark the decoder as wedged for the rest of the session, so multiview and new channels stop creating players that will hang too.
problems.impact: Clear message instead of an endless spinner, and no cascade into the ANR.
problems.risk: A false alarm on a very slow first connection; check ThreadBeat or bytes received before blaming the decoder.

problems.title: Every stop or release flushes the codec first, the step that hung on the MTK decoder
problems.detail: Media3 1.8.0 flushes the video codec before releasing it, and the switch for that is final. A renderer subclass could release first (skip the flush) but must do it only when a release follows. The same disable step also runs when switching channels on the same player, where the flushed decoder is kept for reuse.
problems.evidence: MediaCodecRenderer.onDisabled -> flushOrReleaseCodec -> flushCodec; stack lines 3538-3545; 21:04:10.345 'FlushInputPort() ... WAIT timeout(5 s)'.
problems.fix_idea: [INFERRED] In the live renderer wrapper, set a volatile 'releasing' flag just before calling player.stop() or release(). When the flag is set, the video renderer's onDisabled calls releaseCodec() before super.onDisabled(), so the flush is skipped. Leave channel switching untouched.
problems.impact: One fewer driver round trip on the risky path; may or may not avoid the Idle-transition hang.
problems.risk: Not proven on the Max. Release itself still goes Executing->Idle, which also failed tonight. Needs TV testing, and should be kept to the live player.

problems.title: Reconnecting a stall with stop() throws the decoder away
problems.detail: The retry calls p.stop() when the player is BUFFERING. That releases and re-creates the decoder and can lose the last frame. The ENDED path (seekToDefaultPosition + prepare) kept the decoder through 31 reconnects. But a seek cancels the old connection's load, and a read stuck on a dead socket may take until the 10 s read timeout to finish.
problems.evidence: PlayerHost.kt retry Runnable; ProgressiveMediaPeriod.seekToUs (Loader.cancelLoading); log: 31 reconnects with 2 decoder creations.
problems.fix_idea: [INFERRED] For a TS stall, swap the source instead: setMediaItem(same item) + prepare(). The old period and its loader are dropped at once, and the renderers are not reset, so the decoder and the last frame stay. Keep stop() only as a fallback.
problems.impact: Faster and steadier reconnects, picture held during the gap, fewer decoder creations.
problems.risk: Needs a TV test that a dead connection is really dropped at once this way.

problems.title: The stream 'ending' every ~20 s causes a full recovery each time
problems.detail: When the server closes the connection, the extractor reaches the end, the player goes to ENDED, and recovery takes about 0.8-1.1 s with a decoder flush each time.
problems.evidence: live_evidence.txt 20:35-20:50 'Live recovery: stream ended; try 1 in 300 ms' then 'playing again after 886-1136 ms'; TsExtractor continuity-counter handling (bytecode).
problems.fix_idea: [INFERRED] A small wrapping data source for live TS with no known length: when a read hits the end, reopen the same request at once (limited tries per minute, then pass the end on). The TS reader resyncs on the gap, so the player never sees ENDED.
problems.impact: The 31 visible reconnects tonight would become brief or invisible data gaps.
problems.risk: A real end of channel must still come through (cap the tries). Needs a check against the per-account connection budget (MultiviewLeases / ConnectionBudget).

problems.title: Connections stay open after a wedge
problems.detail: With the playback thread stuck, loaders stop after about 1 MiB and their sockets are never closed (CLOSE_WAIT). The app's connection budget may count them as free while the provider still sees them as open.
problems.evidence: ProgressiveMediaSource.DEFAULT_LOADING_CHECK_INTERVAL_BYTES = 1048576; the incident's ~1.3 MB unread per socket and 3 CLOSE_WAIT sockets.
problems.fix_idea: Once a wedge is detected, open no new streams, and tell the user to restart the Fire TV (which also frees the provider's slots).
problems.impact: Avoids provider refusals and pile-ups after a failure.
problems.risk: Low

problems.title: Multiview's cost cannot be cut by track-selection limits for TS channels
problems.detail: Max video size, bitrate and frame-rate limits only choose variants, so single-rendition TS channels decode at full size. Four 1080p50/60 pictures use about 74-89% of the decoder's declared ceiling. On 1.8.0, each player also runs a 10 ms work loop.
problems.evidence: exceedVideoConstraintsIfNecessary defaults to true; device XML throughput figures; Renderer default 10 ms.
problems.fix_idea: Keep the size limit (it helps HLS). Mute pictures that aren't selected (volume 0, as today); disabling their audio track would save a decoder and an AudioTrack, but switching sound may then force a reconnect (TV test first). Hide removed or off-screen picture SurfaceViews (GONE) so they drop their last buffer. Later, Media3 1.10/1.11 brings video dynamic scheduling, default-on in 1.11; that is a dependency change to weigh separately.
problems.impact: Less CPU and memory while 3-4 pictures play.
problems.risk: Upgrading Media3 is a larger change; audio-track toggling is untested.

problems.title: Decoder reuse when switching channels isn't measured
problems.detail: A reused player still created a new decoder (138 ms at 20:34:24). Likely causes: the new size exceeded the codec's maximum (256) or a larger input buffer was needed (64).
problems.evidence: Timing line 20:34:24.682 'player reused; ... video decoder 138 ms'; MediaCodecVideoRenderer.canReuseCodec / getCodecMaxValues (protected).
problems.fix_idea: Log once per switch the reuse result and discard reasons from onVideoInputFormatChanged. Optionally [INFERRED] raise the live codec's maximum to 1920x1088 (getCodecMaxValues override) so 720p<->1080p switches reuse the decoder.
problems.impact: Faster channel switches and fewer decoder creations.
problems.risk: A 1080p maximum on a 720p channel costs roughly 20 MB more of video buffers.
